$script:AllInOne = $true                    # tells the launcher section not to dot-source \lib
$script:RootFolder = (Get-Location).Path    # ALWAYS the current folder - a second run after cd must not keep the old root


# ===================== BEGIN 01-Config.ps1 =====================

# The launcher (or the all-in-one header) sets $script:RootFolder before loading this file.
# If somebody loads this file on its own, fall back to the current folder.
if (-not $script:RootFolder) { $script:RootFolder = (Get-Location).Path }

$script:Config = @{
    # ---- Folders (relative to the root folder = where Start-OfflinePatcher.ps1 lives) ----
    PatchFolder    = Join-Path $script:RootFolder 'patches'   # drop .msu / .cab files here
    PatchInfoFolder = Join-Path $script:RootFolder 'patches\_info'   # cache: which build each file targets
    LogFolder      = Join-Path $script:RootFolder 'logs'      # one log file per day is written here

    # ---- WinRM ----
    WinRMPort      = 5985        # HTTP WinRM. 5986 would be HTTPS.
    OpenTimeoutSec = 20          # give up on a silent server after this many seconds
    MaxParallel    = 16          # how many servers are checked at the same time

    # ---- Remote staging (on the target server) ----
    RemoteStaging  = 'C:\PatchStaging'   # patch files are copied here before install
    CleanupStaging = $true               # delete the copied file after a successful install
    ProgressEverySec = 45                # while DISM runs, read CBS.log progress this often (one summary line)
    ProgressDetailEveryMin = 5           # ... and one line PER SERVER this often (always, when 3 servers or fewer)
    InstallTimeoutMin = 120              # stop waiting for an install after this long (DISM is NOT killed)

    # ---- Safety thresholds ----
    MinFreeGB      = 5           # refuse to install when C: has less free space than this
    WarnFreeGB     = 10          # show a warning colour below this
    TreatPendingFileRenameAsReboot = $false  # PendingFileRenameOperations is noisy; off by default
    RequireValidSignature  = $true    # a patch must be Authenticode-signed by Microsoft (checked here AND on the server)
    AllowUnknownTargetBuild = $false  # a file whose target build cannot be read is blocked (cannot tell 2019 from 2022)

    # ---- Fun ----
    OperatorName   = 'sys-admin'   # shown in the window title, the banner, the welcome line and a quip
                                   # ("<name>'s Patch Palace") - put the operator's first name here
}

# ---- Shared runtime state (filled in while the tool runs) ----
$script:Operator     = "$env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME"   # who is running the tool - goes into every audit line
$script:Credential   = $null   # PSCredential entered by the operator (kept in memory only, cleared when the GUI closes)
$script:ServerStatus = @{}     # hashtable: server name -> last status object from Get-ServerStatus
$script:Groups       = @()     # output of Get-PatchGroups
$script:Patches      = @()     # output of Get-PatchFiles
$script:Gui          = @{}     # hashtable of WinForms controls, filled by Show-PatcherGui

$script:Banner = @'

  |  _ \ __ _ | |_ ___| |__   |  _ \ __ _| | __ _  ___ ___
  | |_) / _` || __/ __| '_ \  | |_) / _` | |/ _` |/ __/ _ \
  |  __/ (_| || || (__| | | | |  __/ (_| | | (_| | (_|  __/
  |_|   \__,_| \__\___|_| |_| |_|   \__,_|_|\__,_|\___\___|
        Offline Server 2022 patching over WinRM (5985)
'@

# ===================== BEGIN 02-Logging.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  02-Logging.ps1  -  ONE FUNCTION THAT WRITES EVERYWHERE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Every message goes to three places so nothing is ever lost:
#    1. logs\Patcher-YYYYMMDD.log   (permanent record, open it in Notepad)
#    2. the PowerShell console       (colour coded, stays open behind the GUI)
#    3. the log box inside the GUI   (once the GUI exists)
#
#  Levels:  INFO  = normal chatter        OK    = something succeeded
#           WARN  = look at this          ERROR = something failed
#           CMD   = the exact command we are about to run (copy/paste it to
#                   reproduce by hand)   WHY   = explains the reasoning
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  02-Logging.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Changed here:
#  R-18 audit trail - Get-OperatorIdentity is stamped on the session
#  header, every INSTALL / CONFIRM / RESULT / REBOOT line and the event
#  written on the target server.  No password or token is ever logged.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Comments   :
#    -
# =====================================================================

function Get-OperatorIdentity {
    # "CORP\operator" or "CORP\operator (WinRM as CORP\svc-patching)" when alternate credentials are set.
    $who = $script:Operator
    if (-not $who) { $who = "$env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME" }
    if ($script:Credential -and $script:Credential.UserName -ne $who) { $who += " (WinRM as $($script:Credential.UserName))" }
    return $who
}

function Write-PatchLog {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true, Position = 0)][string]$Message,
        [Parameter(Position = 1)][ValidateSet('INFO', 'OK', 'WARN', 'ERROR', 'CMD', 'WHY')][string]$Level = 'INFO'
    )

    $line = '{0} [{1,-5}] {2}' -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'), $Level, $Message

    # 1. File (the folder is created on first use)
    try {
        if (-not (Test-Path -Path $script:Config.LogFolder)) {
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $script:Config.LogFolder -Force | Out-Null
        }
        Add-Content -Path (Get-PatchLogPath) -Value $line -ErrorAction Stop
    } catch {
        Write-Host "Could not write to log file: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
    }

    # 2. Console
    $consoleColour = switch ($Level) {
        'OK'    { 'Green' }
        'WARN'  { 'Yellow' }
        'ERROR' { 'Red' }
        'CMD'   { 'Cyan' }
        'WHY'   { 'DarkGray' }
        default { 'White' }
    }
    Write-Host $line -ForegroundColor $consoleColour

    # 3. GUI log box (only if the GUI has been built and is still open)
    $box = $script:Gui['LogBox']
    if ($box -and -not $box.IsDisposed) {
        $guiColour = switch ($Level) {
            'OK'    { 'Green' }
            'WARN'  { 'DarkOrange' }
            'ERROR' { 'Red' }
            'CMD'   { 'RoyalBlue' }
            'WHY'   { 'Gray' }
            default { 'Black' }
        }
        $box.SelectionStart  = $box.TextLength
        $box.SelectionLength = 0
        $box.SelectionColor  = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromName($guiColour)
        $box.AppendText($line + "`r`n")
        $box.ScrollToCaret()
        # Let the window repaint so the operator sees progress while we are busy.
        [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
    }
}

function Get-PatchLogPath {
    # Today's log file, e.g. logs\Patcher-20261013.log
    return (Join-Path $script:Config.LogFolder ('Patcher-{0}.log' -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd')))
}
# ===================== END 02-Logging.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 03-Groups.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  03-Groups.ps1  -  READ THE SERVER LISTS (PatchGroup-A.txt etc.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Rules for a group file (any *.txt in the root folder):
#    * one server name per line (short name or FQDN)
#    * blank lines are ignored
#    * anything after a # is a comment:   SRV-APP01   # finance app
#    * the file name (without .txt) becomes the group name
#  A .txt file that contains lines that do not look like host names is
#  ignored, so the "code-as-text" copies can never be mistaken for lists.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  03-Groups.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Changed here:
#  R-06 Get-UniqueNames de-duplicates case-insensitively (Select-Object
#  -Unique is case-sensitive in 5.1) and warns when two entries look like
#  the same server (short name vs FQDN); R-26 IP addresses are warned
#  about because they force NTLM instead of Kerberos.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Comments   :
#    -
# =====================================================================

function Test-LooksLikeHostname {
    param([string]$Text)
    # letters, digits, dots and dashes only - that is all a host name can contain
    return ($Text -match '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.\-]*$')
}

function Get-UniqueNames {
    # Case-INsensitive de-duplication that keeps the original order.  (Select-Object -Unique
    # treats SRV01 and srv01 as two different servers in PowerShell 5.1 - that would mean two
    # concurrent installs on one box.)
    param([string[]]$Names)
    $seen = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string] ([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    $out = @()
    foreach ($n in @($Names)) {
        if (-not $n) { continue }
        $t = $n.Trim()
        if ($t -and $seen.Add($t)) { $out += $t }
    }
    return $out
}

function Get-PatchGroups {
    # Returns one object per group:  Name, File, Servers (array of strings)
    $groups = @()
    $files  = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $script:RootFolder -Filter '*.txt' -File | Sort-Object Name)

    foreach ($file in $files) {
        $servers = @()
        $odd     = $null
        foreach ($raw in (Get-Content -Path $file.FullName)) {
            $line = ($raw -split '#')[0].Trim()          # drop comments and whitespace
            if (-not $line) { continue }                  # skip blank lines
            if (-not (Test-LooksLikeHostname $line)) { $odd = $line; break }
            $servers += $line
        }
        if ($odd) {
            Write-PatchLog "Ignoring $($file.Name) - not a server list (first odd line: '$odd')" 'WHY'
            continue
        }
        $servers = @(Get-UniqueNames $servers)
        $groups += [pscustomobject]@{
            Name    = $file.BaseName
            File    = $file.FullName
            Servers = $servers
        }
        Write-PatchLog ("Group '{0}' loaded with {1} server(s) from {2}" -f $file.BaseName, $servers.Count, $file.Name) 'INFO'
        foreach ($s in $servers) {
            if ($s -match '^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$') {
                Write-PatchLog "  -> '$s' is an IP address: WinRM cannot use Kerberos for it and will fall back to NTLM, which needs TrustedHosts on this PC. Use the server's FQDN instead." 'WARN'
            }
        }
        if ($servers.Count -eq 0) {
            Write-PatchLog "  -> $($file.Name) has no servers yet. Open it in Notepad and add one name per line." 'WARN'
        }
    }

    if ($groups.Count -eq 0) {
        Write-PatchLog "No group files found in $script:RootFolder - create e.g. PatchGroup-A.txt with one server per line" 'WARN'
    }
    # Same server written two ways (SRV01 and srv01.corp.local) across the groups?  Say so - the
    # install itself also de-duplicates by the server's real name after the status check.
    $byLabel = @{}
    foreach ($g in $groups) {
        foreach ($s in $g.Servers) {
            $label = ($s -split '\.')[0].ToLower()
            if (-not $byLabel.ContainsKey($label)) { $byLabel[$label] = @() }
            if ($byLabel[$label] -notcontains $s) { $byLabel[$label] += $s }
        }
    }
    foreach ($label in $byLabel.Keys) {
        if ($byLabel[$label].Count -gt 1) { Write-PatchLog ("  -> '{0}' is listed as {1} - probably the same server; it will be patched once" -f $label, ($byLabel[$label] -join ' and ')) 'WARN' }
    }
    $script:Groups = $groups
    return $groups
}

function Get-GroupServers {
    # All unique server names across the given group names ('*' = every group)
    param([string[]]$GroupName = '*')
    $names = @()
    foreach ($g in $script:Groups) {
        if ($GroupName -contains '*' -or $GroupName -contains $g.Name) { $names += $g.Servers }
    }
    return @(Get-UniqueNames $names)
}
# ===================== END 03-Groups.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 04-Patches.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  04-Patches.ps1  -  FIND AND VET THE PATCH FILES IN \patches
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  The tool is fully offline: you download the .msu (or .cab) files from
#  the Microsoft Update Catalog on a machine that has internet, then
#  drop them into the "patches" folder next to the launcher.
#
#  For every file the tool works out, once, and caches in patches\_info:
#    KB number     from the FILE NAME  (windows10.0-kb5122882-x64_....msu -> KB5122882)
#    Target build  from INSIDE the file (expand.exe reads one small XML)   -> 20348 = Server 2022
#    Signature     Get-AuthenticodeSignature: must be Valid and signed by Microsoft
#    SHA256        used to verify the copy on the server and again right before DISM
#  Get-PatchVerdict at the bottom is THE decision "can this KB go on this
#  server?" - the grid cells and the install plan both call it.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  04-Patches.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Fixed here:
#  R-09 no Authenticode check of the .msu; R-11 OS guard failed open when
#  the build could not be read and the _info cache ignored a replaced
#  file; R-12 grid and plan used two different rule orders (now one
#  function, Get-PatchVerdict); R-17 -Path used on file-derived names
#  (now -LiteralPath); R-20 two files with the same KB were not flagged.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Checked    : [ ] read every function   [ ] ran Get-PatchFiles on a real .msu
#               [ ] compared with CODE-REVIEW.md
#  Comments   :
#    -
#    -
# =====================================================================

# Shown by the "Where do I get patches?" button and in the Code Tour.  Edit freely.
$script:PatchHowTo = @'
HOW TO FIND AND DOWNLOAD THIS MONTH'S PATCH  (on a machine that has internet)

1. Find the latest KB number - the update history page is easiest
   Search "Windows Server 2022 update history" or open
   https://support.microsoft.com/help/5005454   (the Server 2022 history hub)
   The left-hand list is newest first, e.g.
      "September 8, 2026 - KB5122882 (OS Build 20348.5622)"
   The top entry WITHOUT the word "Preview" is the current cumulative update (LCU).
   Note the OS Build number: compare it with the Build column in the grid to see
   which servers are already current.
   Numbers only, per Server version:
   https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/release-health/windows-server-release-info

2. Download it from the Microsoft Update Catalog
   Each history article has a "Microsoft Update Catalog" link under
   "How to get this update", or open https://www.catalog.update.microsoft.com
   and search for the KB number, e.g.   KB5122882
   Server 2022 is listed as:
      "Cumulative Update for Microsoft server operating system version 21H2 for x64-based Systems"
   Server 2025 is listed as:
      "... Microsoft server operating system version 24H2 ..."
   Click Download, save the .msu, KEEP THE FILE NAME, copy it into the \patches folder.

3. Sanity checks before you start
   * File name starts with windows10.0-kb... for Server 2022  (windows11.0-kb... = Server 2025).
   * The servicing stack update (SSU) is bundled inside the Server 2022 LCU - one file is enough.
   * .NET Framework updates are separate KBs; add them the same way if they are required.
   * Press "Reload lists + patches" and check the new KB column appears in the grid.
   * The patch list shows the OS the file is for and "UNSIGNED" if the signature is not valid.
'@

function Get-PatchFiles {
    # Returns one object per usable patch file:
    #   Name, FullName, KB, SizeMB, Type, OsLine, TargetBuild, TargetOs, Signature, Signer, Hash
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $script:Config.PatchFolder)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $script:Config.PatchFolder -Force | Out-Null
        Write-PatchLog "Created empty patch folder $($script:Config.PatchFolder)" 'WARN'
    }

    $patches = @()
    $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $script:Config.PatchFolder -File |
               Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.msu', '.cab' } |
               Sort-Object Name)

    foreach ($file in $files) {
        if ($file.Name -match '(?i)(KB\d{6,7})') {
            $kb = $Matches[1].ToUpper()
        } else {
            Write-PatchLog "Skipping '$($file.Name)' - no KB number in the file name. Rename it to include e.g. KB5034770" 'WARN'
            continue
        }
        # "windows10.0-kb..." = Server 2016/2019/2022 line, "windows11.0-kb..." = Windows 11 / Server 2025 line
        $osLine = ''
        if ($file.Name -match '(?i)^(windows\d+\.\d+)') { $osLine = $Matches[1].ToLower() }
        Write-PatchLog ("Patch found: {0}  ({1} MB, {2})" -f $kb, [math]::Round($file.Length / 1MB, 1), $file.Name) 'INFO'

        $info = Get-PatchFileInfo -Path $file.FullName
        $patches += [pscustomobject]@{
            Name        = $file.Name
            FullName    = $file.FullName
            KB          = $kb
            SizeMB      = [math]::Round($file.Length / 1MB, 1)
            Type        = $file.Extension.TrimStart('.').ToLower()
            OsLine      = $osLine
            TargetBuild = $info.TargetBuild
            TargetOs    = (Get-OsNameForBuild -Build $info.TargetBuild)
            Signature   = $info.Signature
            Signer      = $info.Signer
            Hash        = $info.Hash
        }
        if ($info.Signature -ne 'Valid') {
            Write-PatchLog "  -> $kb signature is '$($info.Signature)' (signer: '$($info.Signer)'). It will show as 'Blocked: signature' unless RequireValidSignature is turned off in 01-Config.ps1" 'WARN'
        }
        if ($info.TargetBuild -eq 0) {
            Write-PatchLog "  -> $kb target build could not be read from inside the file. It will show as 'Blocked: OS unknown' unless AllowUnknownTargetBuild is turned on" 'WARN'
        }
    }

    # Two files with one KB (e.g. the .NET CU for 4.8 and 4.8.1) get two identical columns - say so.
    foreach ($group in ($patches | Group-Object KB | Where-Object { $_.Count -gt 1 })) {
        Write-PatchLog ("  -> {0} appears {1} times ({2}). Both columns show the same state; each file is still installed separately." -f $group.Name, $group.Count, (($group.Group | ForEach-Object { $_.Name }) -join ', ')) 'WARN'
    }
    if ($patches.Count -eq 0) {
        Write-PatchLog "No .msu/.cab files in $($script:Config.PatchFolder) - status checks still work, installs need a file" 'WARN'
    }
    $script:Patches = $patches
    return $patches
}

# Known Windows builds (the number BEFORE the dot in 20348.5622) -> friendly names.
$script:BuildNames = @{
    14393 = 'Server 2016'; 17763 = 'Server 2019'; 20348 = 'Server 2022'; 26100 = 'Server 2025 / Win11 24H2'
    19041 = 'Windows 10 2004'; 19042 = 'Windows 10 20H2'; 19043 = 'Windows 10 21H1'; 19044 = 'Windows 10 21H2'; 19045 = 'Windows 10 22H2'
    22000 = 'Windows 11 21H2'; 22621 = 'Windows 11 22H2'; 22631 = 'Windows 11 23H2'
}

function Get-OsNameForBuild {
    param([int]$Build)
    if ($Build -le 0) { return 'unknown' }
    if ($script:BuildNames.ContainsKey($Build)) { return $script:BuildNames[$Build] }
    return "build $Build"
}

function Get-PatchFileInfo {
    # Target build + signature + SHA256 of one file, cached in patches\_info\<file>.txt.
    # The cache is only trusted when the file's size and last-write time still match (a replaced
    # file with the same name is read again).  Reading takes a few seconds for a 600 MB file.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Path)
    $file = Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path
    $infoFolder = $script:Config.PatchInfoFolder
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $infoFolder)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $infoFolder -Force | Out-Null }
    $stamp = '{0}|{1}' -f $file.Length, $file.LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks
    $cache = Join-Path $infoFolder ($file.Name + '.txt')

    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cache) {
        $h = @{}
        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $cache)) { if ($line -match '^([A-Za-z]+)=(.*)$') { $h[$Matches[1]] = $Matches[2] } }
        if ($h['Stamp'] -eq $stamp -and $h['Hash'] -and $h.ContainsKey('TargetBuild') -and $h.ContainsKey('Signature')) {
            return [pscustomobject]@{ TargetBuild = [int]$h['TargetBuild']; Signature = $h['Signature']; Signer = $h['Signer']; Hash = $h['Hash']; Source = $h['Source'] }
        }
    }

    $watch = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    $build = Read-PatchTargetBuild -Path $file.FullName
    # Signature: must be Valid AND signed by Microsoft.  Works offline (the Microsoft roots are in Windows).
    $sigStatus = 'Unknown'; $signer = ''
    try {
        $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature -LiteralPath $file.FullName -ErrorAction Stop
        $sigStatus = [string]$sig.Status
        if ($sig.SignerCertificate) { $signer = $sig.SignerCertificate.Subject }
        if ($sigStatus -eq 'Valid' -and $signer -notmatch 'O=Microsoft Corporation') { $sigStatus = 'ValidButNotMicrosoft' }
    } catch {
        $sigStatus = 'CheckFailed: ' + (Get-ShortError $_)
    }
    $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $secs = [math]::Round($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 1)
    Write-PatchLog ("  -> {0}: target build {1} = {2} (from {3}); signature {4}; SHA256 {5}...  ({6} s, cached in patches\_info)" -f $file.Name, $build.Build, (Get-OsNameForBuild -Build $build.Build), $build.Source, $sigStatus, $hash.Substring(0, 12), $secs) 'INFO'

    @("Stamp=$stamp", "TargetBuild=$($build.Build)", "TargetOs=$(Get-OsNameForBuild -Build $build.Build)", "Source=$($build.Source)",
      "Signature=$sigStatus", "Signer=$signer", "Hash=$hash", "File=$($file.Name)", "Read=$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')") | Set-Content -LiteralPath $cache
    return [pscustomobject]@{ TargetBuild = $build.Build; Signature = $sigStatus; Signer = $signer; Hash = $hash; Source = $build.Source }
}

function Read-PatchTargetBuild {
    # Which Windows build does this file target?  Read OFFLINE from inside the file with
    # expand.exe (part of Windows), in well under a second.
    #   .msu : the small .xml inside names every package with its version, e.g. 20348.5614.1.3;
    #          pkgProperties.txt has Installer Version="10.0.20348.1960"; the bundled servicing
    #          stack cab is called SSU-20348.xxxx-x64.cab.  Any of the three gives the build.
    #   .cab : update.mum inside carries the package version.
    # Returns @{ Build = <int, 0 = unknown>; Source = <where it was read from> }
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Path)
    $file = Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path
    $build = 0
    $how = ''
    $temp = Join-Path $script:Config.PatchInfoFolder ('tmp-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0, 8))
    try {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $temp -Force | Out-Null
        if ($file.Extension -eq '.msu') {
            Write-PatchLog "expand.exe -F:*.xml `"$($file.FullName)`" `"$temp`"   (pulls one small file out of the MSU to read the target build)" 'CMD'
            $null = & expand.exe -F:*.xml "$($file.FullName)" "$temp" 2>&1
            $null = & expand.exe -F:*pkgProperties.txt "$($file.FullName)" "$temp" 2>&1
            foreach ($xml in @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $temp -Filter '*.xml' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $xml.FullName -Raw
                foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($text, 'version="(\d{5})\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+"')) {
                    if ($build -eq 0) { $build = [int]$m.Groups[1].Value; $how = $xml.Name }
                }
            }
            if ($build -eq 0) {
                foreach ($props in @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $temp -Filter '*pkgProperties.txt' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
                    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $props.FullName -Raw
                    if ($text -match 'Installer Version="10\.0\.(\d{5})\.') { $build = [int]$Matches[1]; $how = $props.Name }
                }
            }
            if ($build -eq 0) {
                $listing = (& expand.exe -D "$($file.FullName)" 2>&1) | Out-String
                if ($listing -match 'SSU-(\d{5})\.') { $build = [int]$Matches[1]; $how = 'SSU cab name' }
            }
        } else {
            Write-PatchLog "expand.exe -F:update.mum `"$($file.FullName)`" `"$temp`"" 'CMD'
            $null = & expand.exe -F:update.mum "$($file.FullName)" "$temp" 2>&1
            $mum = Join-Path $temp 'update.mum'
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $mum) {
                $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $mum -Raw
                if ($text -match 'version="(\d{5})\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+"') { $build = [int]$Matches[1]; $how = 'update.mum' }
            }
        }
    } catch {
        Write-PatchLog "Could not read the target build of $($file.Name): $(Get-ShortError $_)" 'WARN'
    } finally {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temp -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    if ($build -eq 0) { $how = 'not found' }
    return @{ Build = $build; Source = $how }
}

function Test-PatchOsMismatch {
    # $true when the file is for a different Windows build than the server runs.
    #   Best    : TargetBuild read from inside the file  vs  the server's build (20348 = 2022, 17763 = 2019)
    #   Fallback: the file-name line - "windows10.0" = Server 2016/2019/2022, "windows11.0" = Win11 / Server 2025
    #             (cannot tell 2019 from 2022 - that is why an unknown build is blocked by default)
    param($Status, $Patch)
    if (-not $Status.Build) { return $false }
    $major = 0
    [void][int]::TryParse(($Status.Build -split '\.')[0], [ref]$major)
    if ($major -eq 0) { return $false }
    if ($Patch.TargetBuild -gt 0) {
        $a = $Patch.TargetBuild; $b = $major
        if ($a -in 22621, 22631 -and $b -in 22621, 22631) { return $false }   # Win11 22H2/23H2 share packages
        return ($a -ne $b)
    }
    if (-not $Patch.OsLine) { return $false }
    if ($Patch.OsLine -eq 'windows10.0' -and $major -ge 22000) { return $true }
    if ($Patch.OsLine -eq 'windows11.0' -and $major -lt 22000) { return $true }
    return $false
}

function Get-OsMismatchText {
    # Human wording for the plan and the log.
    param($Status, $Patch)
    if ($Patch.TargetBuild -gt 0) {
        return ("wrong OS - file is for {0} (build {1}), server is build {2}" -f $Patch.TargetOs, $Patch.TargetBuild, $Status.Build)
    }
    return ("wrong OS line - file is '{0}', server build is {1}" -f $Patch.OsLine, $Status.Build)
}

function Get-PatchVerdict {
    # THE single "can this KB go on this server?" decision.  The grid cell (Get-PatchCellText)
    # and the install plan (New-PatchPlan) both call it, so they can never disagree.
    # Order: not checked / unreachable / already installed / pending reboot / busy servicing /
    #        low disk / bad signature / OS unknown / wrong OS / READY
    param($Status, $Patch)
    $v = [pscustomobject]@{ Go = $false; Cell = ''; Reason = '' }
    if (-not $Status)                                 { $v.Cell = 'not checked';         $v.Reason = 'not checked yet'; return $v }
    if (-not $Status.Reachable)                       { $v.Cell = '?';                   $v.Reason = 'unreachable - see log'; return $v }
    if ($Status.HotFixIDs -contains $Patch.KB)        { $v.Cell = 'Installed';           $v.Reason = 'already installed'; return $v }
    if ($Status.HistoryInstalledKBs -contains $Patch.KB) { $v.Cell = 'Installed (history)'; $v.Reason = 'already installed (per Windows Update history)'; return $v }
    if ($Status.PendingReboot)                        { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: reboot';     $v.Reason = "pending reboot ($($Status.RebootReasons)) - reboot first"; return $v }
    if ($Status.ServicingActive)                      { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: servicing';  $v.Reason = "servicing already running on the server ($($Status.ServicingReasons)) - wait and re-check"; return $v }
    if ($Status.FreeGB -lt $script:Config.MinFreeGB)  { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: disk';       $v.Reason = "low disk ($($Status.FreeGB) GB free on C:)"; return $v }
    if ($script:Config.RequireValidSignature -and $Patch.Signature -ne 'Valid') { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: signature'; $v.Reason = "file signature is '$($Patch.Signature)' - not a valid Microsoft-signed package"; return $v }
    if ($Patch.TargetBuild -le 0 -and -not $script:Config.AllowUnknownTargetBuild) { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: OS unknown'; $v.Reason = 'target build could not be read from inside the file - see patches\_info and the log'; return $v }
    if (Test-PatchOsMismatch -Status $Status -Patch $Patch) { $v.Cell = 'Blocked: wrong OS'; $v.Reason = (Get-OsMismatchText -Status $Status -Patch $Patch); return $v }
    $v.Go = $true; $v.Cell = 'READY'; $v.Reason = 'ready'
    return $v
}
# ===================== END 04-Patches.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 05-WinRM.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  05-WinRM.ps1  -  TALKING TO THE SERVERS OVER WinRM (TCP 5985)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Three kinds of call are used, from "no auth" to "full auth":
#    Test-WSMan      -> anonymous "identify" request. Proves the port and
#                       the WinRM service are alive. No credentials needed
#                       (this is why winrm get/enumerate worked without auth).
#    Invoke-Command  -> runs a script block ON the server. Uses your current
#                       Kerberos login, or $script:Credential if you set one.
#    New-PSSession   -> a persistent connection used for copying files
#                       (Copy-FileToSession) and the install job.
#
#  Credentials are ONLY asked for in the foreground, with Get-Credential,
#  when a server says "Access is denied" or when you click "Set credentials".
#  Use FQDNs in the group files so Kerberos can find the service; never set
#  TrustedHosts=* to "fix" an authentication error.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  05-WinRM.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Fixed here:
#  R-05 status now reports servicing-in-progress and the extra reboot
#  keys (RebootInProgress, PostRebootReporting, UpdateExeVolatile,
#  computer rename); R-06 names de-duplicated case-insensitively; R-08
#  job wait loops treated any non-Running state as finished; R-17
#  -LiteralPath for file-derived paths; R-21 copy gave up after five
#  halvings with a misleading error; R-22 remote SHA256 computed even
#  when sizes differed; R-23 a corrupt staged file was left behind after
#  a failed verification; R-24 credential prompt could open behind the
#  GUI (form is re-activated afterwards).
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Checked    : [ ] read every function   [ ] ran a status check   [ ] ran a copy
#               [ ] compared with CODE-REVIEW.md
#  Comments   :
#    -
#    -
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  This script block is sent to each server and RUNS THERE.
#  It must be self contained: no functions or variables from this tool
#  exist on the remote side, only what is passed via -ArgumentList.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
$script:RemoteStatusScript = {
    param([bool]$TreatPfroAsReboot)
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

    # Operating system, build and last boot
    $os = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem
    $cv = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion'
    $ubr = $cv.UBR
    if (-not $ubr) { $ubr = 0 }

    # Free space on C: (patches need room to stage and install)
    $disk = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DeviceID='C:'"

    # Installed updates, read TWO ways:
    #  1. Get-HotFix (Win32_QuickFixEngineering): only the CBS packages still present.  Each new
    #     cumulative update supersedes the previous one, which then drops off this list, so a
    #     well patched server shows only a handful of entries here.  This is the primary source.
    #  2. Windows Update Agent history (the same list as Settings > Update history): every
    #     install the server has ever done, including superseded, failed and Defender updates.
    #     Read offline from the local WUA database via COM - nothing goes to the internet.
    # Nested objects get flattened to text by remoting, so both lists are sent as ready-made lines.
    $hotfixes = @(Get-HotFix)
    $withDate = @($hotfixes | Where-Object { $_.InstalledOn } | Sort-Object InstalledOn)
    # "Newest hotfixes" = EVERY Get-HotFix entry from the most recent install date.  The cumulative
    # update and the .NET cumulative update normally land on the same day, so one KB alone would be
    # misleading.  The Build number (UBR) is the real patch level; this column is only a hint.
    $lastText = 'none'
    if ($withDate.Count -gt 0) {
        $newestDate = $withDate[-1].InstalledOn.Date
        $sameDay = @($withDate | Where-Object { $_.InstalledOn.Date -eq $newestDate } | ForEach-Object { $_.HotFixID } | Sort-Object -Unique)
        $more = ''
        if ($sameDay.Count -gt 3) { $more = ' +{0}' -f ($sameDay.Count - 3) }
        $lastText = '{0}{1} ({2:yyyy-MM-dd})' -f (@($sameDay | Select-Object -First 3) -join ' + '), $more, $newestDate
    }
    $hotfixLines = @($hotfixes | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending | ForEach-Object {
        $d = 'unknown date'
        if ($_.InstalledOn) { $d = $_.InstalledOn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') }
        '{0,-10}  {1,-12}  {2,-24}  {3}' -f $_.HotFixID, $d, $_.Description, $_.InstalledBy
    })

    $historyLines = @()
    $historyInstalled = @()
    $historyCount = 0
    $historyError = ''
    try {
        $wuSession  = New-Object -ComObject 'Microsoft.Update.Session'
        $wuSearcher = $wuSession.CreateUpdateSearcher()
        $historyCount = [int]$wuSearcher.GetTotalHistoryCount()
        if ($historyCount -gt 0) {
            $take = [math]::Min($historyCount, 80)
            $seen = @{}
            foreach ($entry in $wuSearcher.QueryHistory(0, $take)) {
                if (-not $entry.Title) { continue }
                $kb = ''
                if ($entry.Title -match '(?i)(KB\d{6,7})') { $kb = $Matches[1].ToUpper() }
                $result = 'Code ' + $entry.ResultCode
                switch ([int]$entry.ResultCode) {
                    1 { $result = 'In progress' }
                    2 { $result = 'Succeeded' }
                    3 { $result = 'Succeeded w/errors' }
                    4 { $result = 'Failed' }
                    5 { $result = 'Aborted' }
                }
                $op = 'Install'
                if ([int]$entry.Operation -eq 2) { $op = 'Uninstall' }
                $when = ''
                if ($entry.Date) { $when = ([datetime]$entry.Date).ToLocalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') }
                $historyLines += '{0,-16}  {1,-9}  {2,-18}  {3,-10}  {4}' -f $when, $op, $result, $kb, $entry.Title
                # newest entry per KB decides whether it counts as installed
                if ($kb -and -not $seen.ContainsKey($kb)) {
                    $seen[$kb] = $true
                    if ($op -eq 'Install' -and $result -like 'Succeeded*') { $historyInstalled += $kb }
                }
            }
        }
    } catch {
        $historyError = $_.Exception.Message
    }

    # Pending reboot - the HARD flags, every one of them counted:
    $reasons = @()
    $cbs = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing'
    foreach ($k in 'RebootPending', 'PackagesPending', 'RebootInProgress') { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath "$cbs\$k") { $reasons += "CBS:$k" } }
    foreach ($k in 'RebootRequired', 'PostRebootReporting') { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\$k") { $reasons += "WU:$k" } }
    $vol = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Updates' -Name UpdateExeVolatile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).UpdateExeVolatile
    if ($vol -and $vol -ne 0) { $reasons += 'UpdateExeVolatile' }
    $activeName = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ActiveComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    $wantedName = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    if ($activeName -and $wantedName -and $activeName -ne $wantedName) { $reasons += 'ComputerRename' }
    # PendingFileRenameOperations (PFRO): a list of files Windows must rename/delete at the next boot
    # because they were locked.  Installers and anti-virus products add to it all the time and it is
    # often left behind, so on its own it is a WEAK sign.  Shown, but not counted, unless the operator
    # sets TreatPendingFileRenameAsReboot = $true in 01-Config.ps1.
    $pfro = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager' -Name PendingFileRenameOperations -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).PendingFileRenameOperations
    $pfroPresent = [bool]$pfro
    $pfroEntries = @()
    if ($pfroPresent) {
        $pfroEntries = @($pfro | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { $_ -replace '^\\\?\?\\', '' } | Select-Object -First 15)
    }
    if ($pfroPresent -and $TreatPfroAsReboot) { $reasons += 'PendingFileRenameOperations' }

    # Is somebody servicing this box RIGHT NOW?  (another admin, Windows Update, a previous run)
    # dism.exe / wusa.exe present = yes.  TiWorker.exe alone is NOT enough: it idles for minutes after routine
    # maintenance, so it only counts while it is actually burning CPU (sampled over 2 s), and the Windows
    # Update agent is asked directly whether it is installing.  Same block in RemoteInstallScript/RemoteRebootScript.
    $busy = @(Get-Process -Name dism, wusa -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.ProcessName } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $ti = @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    if ($ti.Count -gt 0) {
        $cpu1 = 0.0; foreach ($p in $ti) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu1 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
        $cpu2 = 0.0; foreach ($p in @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu2 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
        if (($cpu2 - $cpu1) -ge 0.25) { $busy += ('TiWorker busy ({0:N1} s CPU in 2 s)' -f ($cpu2 - $cpu1)) }
    }
    try { if ((New-Object -ComObject 'Microsoft.Update.Session').CreateUpdateInstaller().IsBusy) { $busy += 'Windows Update agent installing' } } catch { }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer      = $env:COMPUTERNAME
        Caption       = $os.Caption
        Build         = '{0}.{1}' -f $cv.CurrentBuildNumber, $ubr
        LastBoot      = $os.LastBootUpTime
        UptimeDays    = [math]::Round(((Get-Date) - $os.LastBootUpTime).TotalDays, 1)
        FreeGB        = [math]::Round($disk.FreeSpace / 1GB, 1)
        PendingReboot = ($reasons.Count -gt 0)
        RebootReasons = ($reasons -join ', ')
        PfroPresent   = $pfroPresent
        PfroEntries   = $pfroEntries
        PfroCount     = @($pfro | Where-Object { $_ }).Count
        ServicingActive  = ($busy.Count -gt 0)
        ServicingReasons = ($busy -join ', ')
        HotFixIDs     = @($hotfixes | ForEach-Object { $_.HotFixID })
        HotFixLines   = $hotfixLines
        HistoryInstalledKBs = $historyInstalled
        HistoryLines  = $historyLines
        HistoryCount  = $historyCount
        HistoryError  = $historyError
        LastHotFix    = $lastText
        PSVersion     = $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()
    }
}

function New-PatcherSessionOption {
    # OpenTimeout = how long to wait for a server that does not answer before giving up.
    return (New-PSSessionOption -OpenTimeout ($script:Config.OpenTimeoutSec * 1000))
}

function Get-ConnectionArgs {
    # A "splat" hashtable so every WinRM call is built the same way: @conn
    $splat = @{
        Port          = $script:Config.WinRMPort
        SessionOption = (New-PatcherSessionOption)
    }
    if ($script:Credential) { $splat['Credential'] = $script:Credential }
    return $splat
}

function Get-PatcherCredential {
    # Foreground credential prompt (Windows dialog), running as the logged-on user.
    # The dialog belongs to the console window, which can sit BEHIND the GUI - the status bar says so,
    # and the GUI is brought back to the front afterwards.
    param([string]$Reason = 'alternate credentials for WinRM')
    Write-PatchLog "Prompting for credentials in the foreground: $Reason  (look for the Windows credential dialog - it may be behind this window)" 'WHY'
    Set-GuiStatus 'Credential prompt open - it may be behind this window'
    $cred = Get-Credential -Message "Offline Patcher - $Reason" -UserName "$env:USERDOMAIN\"
    $form = $script:Gui['Form']
    if ($form -and -not $form.IsDisposed) { try { $form.Activate() } catch { } }
    if ($cred -and $cred.UserName -and $cred.UserName -ne "$env:USERDOMAIN\") {
        $script:Credential = $cred
        Write-PatchLog "Credentials stored in memory for $($cred.UserName) (never written to disk) by $env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME" 'OK'
        return $true
    }
    Write-PatchLog 'Credential prompt cancelled - still using the current Windows login' 'WARN'
    return $false
}

function Clear-PatcherCredential {
    $script:Credential = $null
    Write-PatchLog 'Stored credentials cleared - back to the current Windows login' 'INFO'
}

function Test-ServerWinRM {
    # The "no authentication" check. Good first step when a server shows as unreachable.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$ComputerName)
    Write-PatchLog "Test-WSMan -ComputerName $ComputerName -Port $($script:Config.WinRMPort)" 'CMD'
    try {
        $r = Test-WSMan -ComputerName $ComputerName -Port $script:Config.WinRMPort -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-PatchLog "$ComputerName answers on WinRM (stack $($r.ProductVersion))" 'OK'
        return $true
    } catch {
        Write-PatchLog "$ComputerName did NOT answer on $($script:Config.WinRMPort): $(Get-ShortError $_)" 'ERROR'
        return $false
    }
}

function Get-ShortError {
    # The exception message in full, but on ONE line (PowerShell's own multi-line
    # "+ CategoryInfo" noise is left out) so the log stays easy to read and grep.
    param($ErrorRecord)
    $msg = ''
    if ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) { $msg = $ErrorRecord.Exception.Message }
    elseif ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Exception]) { $msg = $ErrorRecord.Message }
    else { $msg = [string]$ErrorRecord }
    $lines = @($msg -split "`r?`n" | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ })
    return ($lines -join ' | ')
}

function Get-ErrorLocation {
    # "file.ps1: line 123" for a caught error.  In all-in-one (Invoke-Expression) mode there is no
    # file, so it reads "<No file>: line N" where N counts from the top of the all-in-one text.
    param($ErrorRecord)
    if ($ErrorRecord.ScriptStackTrace) { return (($ErrorRecord.ScriptStackTrace -split "`r?`n")[0] -replace '^at ', '') }
    return ''
}

function New-UnreachableStatus {
    # Same shape as the remote object so the GUI never trips over a missing property.
    param([string]$ComputerName, [string]$Reason)
    return [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer = $ComputerName; Caption = ''; Build = ''; LastBoot = $null; UptimeDays = $null
        FreeGB = $null; PendingReboot = $false; RebootReasons = ''; PfroPresent = $false; PfroEntries = @(); PfroCount = 0
        ServicingActive = $false; ServicingReasons = ''
        HotFixIDs = @(); HotFixLines = @(); HistoryInstalledKBs = @(); HistoryLines = @(); HistoryCount = 0; HistoryError = ''
        LastHotFix = ''; PSVersion = ''
        Reachable = $false; Error = $Reason; Checked = (Get-Date)
    }
}

function Wait-PatcherJob {
    # Waits for a job while keeping the GUI alive (DoEvents) and the status bar ticking.
    # "Finished" means Completed / Failed / Stopped / Disconnected - NotStarted, Blocked and
    # Suspending (robust-connection retries after a network blip) are still "in progress".
    param($Job, [string]$Activity = 'Working', [int]$TimeoutSec = 3600)
    $finished = @('Completed', 'Failed', 'Stopped', 'Disconnected')
    $watch = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    while ($finished -notcontains $Job.State -and $watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -lt $TimeoutSec) {
        Set-GuiStatus ('{0} ... {1}s' -f $Activity, [int]$watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
    }
    if ($finished -notcontains $Job.State) {
        Write-PatchLog "$Activity timed out after $TimeoutSec s - stopping the job" 'ERROR'
        Stop-Job -Job $Job
    }
}

function Set-GuiStatus {
    # Updates the status bar text if the GUI exists; harmless from the console.
    param([string]$Text)
    $label = $script:Gui['StatusLabel']
    if ($label) {
        $label.Text = $Text
        [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
    }
}

function Set-GuiProgress {
    # Patch-o-meter: -Percent 0..100 shows a real bar, -Marquee goes back to "busy, unknown length".
    param([int]$Percent = -1, [switch]$Marquee)
    $bar = $script:Gui['Progress']
    if (-not $bar) { return }
    if ($Marquee) { $bar.Style = 'Marquee'; return }
    $bar.Style = 'Continuous'
    if ($Percent -lt 0) { $Percent = 0 }
    if ($Percent -gt 100) { $Percent = 100 }
    $bar.Value = $Percent
    [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
}

function Get-ServerStatus {
    # Checks many servers at once (one child job per server) and stores the
    # result in $script:ServerStatus[name].  Returns the array of status objects.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$ComputerName,
        [switch]$NoRetry       # internal: stops the "prompt for credentials and retry" loop
    )
    $names = @(Get-UniqueNames $ComputerName)
    if ($names.Count -eq 0) { return @() }

    $conn = Get-ConnectionArgs
    $who  = 'current login'
    if ($script:Credential) { $who = $script:Credential.UserName }
    Write-PatchLog ("Invoke-Command -ComputerName {0} -Port {1} -AsJob  (status script, as {2})" -f ($names -join ','), $conn.Port, $who) 'CMD'

    $call = @{
        ComputerName  = $names
        ScriptBlock   = $script:RemoteStatusScript
        ArgumentList  = $script:Config.TreatPendingFileRenameAsReboot
        ThrottleLimit = $script:Config.MaxParallel
        AsJob         = $true
        ErrorAction   = 'SilentlyContinue'
    }
    $job = Invoke-Command @call @conn
    Wait-PatcherJob -Job $job -Activity ("Checking {0} server(s)" -f $names.Count) -TimeoutSec 600

    $results = @()
    $denied  = @()
    foreach ($child in $job.ChildJobs) {
        $name = $child.Location
        $jobErrors = @()
        $out = Receive-Job -Job $child -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -ErrorVariable jobErrors
        $status = $null
        if ($out) {
            $status = $out | Select-Object -First 1
            $status | Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reachable -NotePropertyValue $true  -Force
            $status | Add-Member -NotePropertyName Error     -NotePropertyValue ''     -Force
            $status | Add-Member -NotePropertyName Checked   -NotePropertyValue (Get-Date) -Force
            $flag = 'no reboot pending'
            if ($status.PendingReboot) { $flag = "PENDING REBOOT ($($status.RebootReasons))" }
            if ($status.ServicingActive) { $flag += ", SERVICING ACTIVE ($($status.ServicingReasons))" }
            Write-PatchLog ("{0}: build {1}, {2} GB free, up {3} d, {4}, newest hotfixes {5}" -f $name, $status.Build, $status.FreeGB, $status.UptimeDays, $flag, $status.LastHotFix) 'OK'
        } else {
            $reason = 'no data returned'
            if ($jobErrors.Count -gt 0) { $reason = Get-ShortError $jobErrors[0] }
            elseif ($child.JobStateInfo.Reason) { $reason = Get-ShortError $child.JobStateInfo.Reason }
            $status = New-UnreachableStatus -ComputerName $name -Reason $reason
            if ($reason -match 'Access is denied') { $denied += $name }
            Write-PatchLog "$name FAILED: $reason" 'ERROR'
        }
        $script:ServerStatus[$name] = $status
        $results += $status
    }
    Remove-Job -Job $job -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    # Access denied with the current login?  Ask once (foreground) and retry just those servers.
    if ($denied.Count -gt 0 -and -not $NoRetry -and -not $script:Credential) {
        Write-PatchLog ("{0} server(s) refused the current login - offering a credential prompt" -f $denied.Count) 'WHY'
        if (Get-PatcherCredential -Reason "access denied on $($denied -join ', ')") {
            $retried = Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $denied -NoRetry
            foreach ($r in $retried) { $results = @($results | Where-Object { $_.Computer -ne $r.Computer }) + $r }
        }
    }
    Set-GuiStatus 'Status check finished'
    return $results
}

# =====================================================================
#  COPYING A FILE OVER WinRM - IN SLICES
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Every WinRM request has to fit inside the server's "MaxEnvelopeSizekb"
#  (default 500 KB).  Copy-Item -ToSession in PowerShell 5.1 sends bigger
#  requests than that and fails with "...exceeded the configured
#  MaxEnvelopeSize quota".  So we do it ourselves: read the file in slices,
#  Base64 each slice (that makes it 37% bigger), send it as an argument to a
#  tiny script block that appends it on the server.  The slice size is worked
#  out from the server's own MaxEnvelopeSizekb (500 -> 224 KB slices), the
#  copy can resume, and the result is verified with a SHA256 hash on both sides.
# =====================================================================

# RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER: what is there already, and how big may a request be?
$script:RemoteFileInfoScript = {
    param([string]$Path, [bool]$WithHash)
    $r = [pscustomobject]@{ Exists = $false; Length = -1; Hash = ''; EnvelopeKB = 500 }
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) {
        $r.Exists = $true
        $r.Length = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path).Length
        if ($WithHash) { $r.Hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $Path -Algorithm SHA256).Hash }
    }
    # How big may one request be?  Try the WSMan provider, then winrm.cmd, else assume the default 500.
    $kb = 0
    try { $kb = [int](Get-Item -Path 'WSMan:\localhost\MaxEnvelopeSizekb' -ErrorAction Stop).Value } catch { }
    if ($kb -le 0) {
        try {
            $line = @(& winrm.cmd get winrm/config 2>$null | Where-Object { $_ -match 'MaxEnvelopeSizekb\s*=\s*(\d+)' })
            if ($line.Count -gt 0 -and $line[0] -match 'MaxEnvelopeSizekb\s*=\s*(\d+)') { $kb = [int]$Matches[1] }
        } catch { }
    }
    if ($kb -le 0) { $kb = 500 }
    $r.EnvelopeKB = $kb
    return $r
}

# RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER: appends one slice (Create on the first slice) and returns the new length.
$script:RemoteWriteSliceScript = {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Base64, [bool]$FirstSlice)
    $bytes = [System.Convert]::FromBase64String($Base64)
    $mode = [System.IO.FileMode]::Append
    if ($FirstSlice) {
        $mode = [System.IO.FileMode]::Create
        $folder = Split-Path -Path $Path -Parent
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $folder)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $folder -Force | Out-Null }
    }
    $fs = New-Object System.IO.FileStream($Path, $mode, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write)
    try { $fs.Write($bytes, 0, $bytes.Length) } finally { $fs.Close() }
    return (Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path).Length
}

# RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER: throws away a staged file that failed verification.
$script:RemoteDeleteScript = {
    param([string]$Path)
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $Path -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

function Invoke-RemoteBlock {
    # Runs a script block inside the session - or locally when there is no session,
    # which lets the copy logic be tested on one machine (see the Code Tour).
    param($Session, [scriptblock]$ScriptBlock, [object[]]$ArgumentList)
    if ($Session) { return (Invoke-Command -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $ScriptBlock -ArgumentList $ArgumentList -ErrorAction Stop) }
    return (& $ScriptBlock @ArgumentList)
}

function Copy-FileToSession {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Path,          # local file
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Destination,   # full path on the server
        $Session,                                              # PSSession; $null = local self-test
        [int]$SliceKB = 0,                                     # 0 = derive from the server's MaxEnvelopeSizekb
        [string]$LocalHash = ''                                # SHA256 if already known (saves hashing a big file again)
    )
    $local = Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path
    $label = 'local'
    if ($Session) { $label = $Session.ComputerName }
    $totalMB = [math]::Round($local.Length / 1MB, 1)
    if (-not $LocalHash) { $LocalHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $Path -Algorithm SHA256).Hash }

    # 1. Is it already there?  Only hash the remote file when the sizes match (hashing a partial file is wasted work).
    $info = Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteFileInfoScript -ArgumentList $Destination, $false
    $offset = 0
    if ($info.Exists -and $info.Length -eq $local.Length) {
        Set-GuiStatus "$label - $($local.Name) already staged, checking its hash..."
        $info = Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteFileInfoScript -ArgumentList $Destination, $true
        if ($LocalHash -eq $info.Hash) {
            Write-PatchLog "$label - $($local.Name) is already there and the SHA256 matches - no copy needed" 'OK'
            return $true
        }
        Write-PatchLog "$label - a file of the same size is there but its hash differs - copying again from the start" 'WARN'
    } elseif ($info.Exists -and $info.Length -gt 0 -and $info.Length -lt $local.Length) {
        $offset = $info.Length
        Write-PatchLog ("{0} - a partial copy ({1} MB) is there - resuming from that point (the final hash check catches a bad one)" -f $label, [math]::Round($offset / 1MB, 1)) 'INFO'
    }

    # 2. Slice size: 65% of the envelope, shrunk by the Base64 overhead, rounded to 16 KB.
    if ($SliceKB -le 0) {
        $SliceKB = [int]([math]::Floor($info.EnvelopeKB * 0.65 / 1.37 / 16) * 16)
        if ($SliceKB -lt 32) { $SliceKB = 32 }
        if ($SliceKB -gt 4096) { $SliceKB = 4096 }
    }
    $trips = [math]::Ceiling(($local.Length - $offset) / ($SliceKB * 1024))
    Write-PatchLog ("{0} - MaxEnvelopeSizekb on the server is {1}, so {2} MB goes over in {3} KB slices = {4} round trips" -f $label, $info.EnvelopeKB, $totalMB, $SliceKB, $trips) 'WHY'
    if ($info.EnvelopeKB -le 1024 -and -not $script:EnvelopeTipShown) {
        Write-PatchLog '   tip: on the servers  winrm set winrm/config @{MaxEnvelopeSizekb="8192"}  makes copies many times faster (shown once per run)' 'WHY'
        $script:EnvelopeTipShown = $true
    }

    # 3. Send the slices.  If the server still says the request is too big, halve the slice and carry on.
    $watch = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    $lastTick = -10
    $completed = $false
    for ($attempt = 1; $attempt -le 6; $attempt++) {
        $fs = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($Path)
        try {
            $fs.Position = $offset
            $sent = $offset
            $first = ($offset -eq 0)
            $buffer = New-Object byte[] ($SliceKB * 1024)
            while (($read = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)) -gt 0) {
                $b64 = [System.Convert]::ToBase64String($buffer, 0, $read)
                $remoteLength = Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteWriteSliceScript -ArgumentList $Destination, $b64, $first
                $first = $false
                $sent += $read
                if ([long]$remoteLength -ne $sent) { throw "The server reports $remoteLength bytes but $sent were sent - aborting the copy" }
                if ($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds - $lastTick -ge 2) {
                    $lastTick = $watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds
                    $rate = 0
                    if ($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -gt 0) { $rate = [math]::Round(($sent - $offset) / 1MB / $watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 1) }
                    Set-GuiStatus ("Copying {0} to {1}: {2} / {3} MB  ({4} MB/s)" -f $local.Name, $label, [math]::Round($sent / 1MB), $totalMB, $rate)
                    Set-GuiProgress -Percent ([int](100 * $sent / $local.Length))
                }
            }
            $completed = $true
            break
        } catch {
            $msg = Get-ShortError $_
            if ($msg -match 'MaxEnvelopeSize' -and $SliceKB -gt 32) {
                $SliceKB = [int]($SliceKB / 2)
                $again = Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteFileInfoScript -ArgumentList $Destination, $false
                $offset = 0
                if ($again.Exists -and $again.Length -gt 0) { $offset = $again.Length }
                Write-PatchLog ("{0} - the server rejected a slice as too big; retrying with {1} KB slices from {2} MB (attempt {3})" -f $label, $SliceKB, [math]::Round($offset / 1MB, 1), ($attempt + 1)) 'WARN'
            } else {
                throw
            }
        } finally {
            $fs.Close()
        }
    }
    Set-GuiProgress -Marquee
    if (-not $completed) { throw "$label - the server kept rejecting slices as too big (last size $SliceKB KB). Check MaxEnvelopeSizekb on the server: winrm get winrm/config" }

    # 4. Verify: size and SHA256 must match on both sides.  A bad copy is deleted so the next run starts clean.
    Set-GuiStatus "$label - verifying the copy (SHA256)..."
    $final = Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteFileInfoScript -ArgumentList $Destination, $true
    if ($final.Length -ne $local.Length -or $final.Hash -ne $LocalHash) {
        Invoke-RemoteBlock -Session $Session -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteDeleteScript -ArgumentList $Destination | Out-Null
        throw "Copy verification FAILED on $label - size $($final.Length) vs $($local.Length), hash match = $($final.Hash -eq $LocalHash). The staged file was deleted; run the install again."
    }
    $secs = [math]::Round($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)
    $rate = 0
    if ($secs -gt 0) { $rate = [math]::Round(($local.Length - $offset) / 1MB / $secs, 1) }
    Write-PatchLog ("{0} - copy finished: {1} MB in {2} s ({3} MB/s), SHA256 verified" -f $label, $totalMB, $secs, $rate) 'OK'
    return $true
}
# ===================== END 05-WinRM.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 06-Install.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  06-Install.ps1  -  INSTALLING A PATCH OVER WinRM
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  The flow (see Install-PatchOnServers at the bottom):
#    1. Fresh status check of the chosen servers (never trust old data)
#    2. Build a plan: which KB goes to which server, and why not
#    3. Show the plan                          -> OK / Cancel
#    4. SAFETY POP-UP 1: VMware snapshot taken? -> No = abort
#    5. SAFETY POP-UP 2: Trellix in maintenance mode? -> No = abort
#    6. Status check AGAIN (the pop-ups may have been open for a while),
#       then per server: PSSession, locked-down C:\PatchStaging, slice copy
#    7. Start the install script block on every server at once (-AsJob)
#    8. Wait (GUI stays alive, progress every 45 s), collect the results
#    9. Fresh status check again so the grid shows the new truth
#
#  WHY DISM AND NOT WUSA?  wusa.exe refuses to run inside a remote
#  (WinRM) session - it fails with "access denied"/exit code 5.  DISM is
#  happy to run remotely, so we unpack the .msu with expand.exe and feed
#  the .cab inside it to  dism /Online /Add-Package.
#
#  RULE FOR EVERY POP-UP IN THIS FILE: a MessageBox RETURNS a value.  If
#  that value is not captured it leaks into the function's output and a
#  "return $false" silently becomes "@('OK', $false)" = true.  So every
#  pop-up whose answer we do not need is written as  $null = Show-...
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  06-Install.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (two reviewers, see CODE-REVIEW.md).
#  Findings fixed in this file: R-01 safety pop-up "No" did not abort
#  (MessageBox result leaked into the return value); R-02 "nothing to do"
#  reported as a failed install; R-03 Reboot button had no pending-reboot
#  or servicing guard; R-04 timeout killed DISM mid-install; R-05 stale
#  status at install time + no servicing guard on the server; R-06 same
#  server twice (case / FQDN); R-07 staging folder writable by Users and
#  no hash re-check before expand; R-10 per-package results; R-13 KB in
#  failure rows; R-14 sessions leaked on error; R-15 reboot reported as
#  failed; R-16 pop-ups taller than the screen; R-19 remote path built
#  with local Join-Path; R-20 two files with one KB shared a folder.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Checked    : [ ] read every function   [ ] ran it against a test server
#               [ ] compared with CODE-REVIEW.md   [ ] safety pop-ups answered No
#  Comments   :
#    -
#    -
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER before anything is copied: makes sure the
#  staging folder is a real folder owned by admins, with an ACL that
#  ordinary users cannot write to (C:\ lets Users create folders).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
$script:RemoteStagingScript = {
    param([string]$Staging)
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Staging) {
        $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $Staging -Force
        if ($item.Attributes -band [System.IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) { throw "$Staging is a junction or symbolic link - refusing to use it" }
        if (-not $item.PSIsContainer) { throw "$Staging exists but is a file" }
        $owner = (Get-Acl -LiteralPath $Staging).Owner
        if ($owner -notmatch 'Administrators|SYSTEM|TrustedInstaller') { throw "$Staging is owned by '$owner', not by Administrators - refusing to use it" }
    } else {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Staging -Force | Out-Null
    }
    # SYSTEM and Administrators only; inheritance from C:\ removed.
    $null = & icacls.exe "$Staging" /inheritance:r /grant:r '*S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F' '*S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F' 2>&1
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "icacls could not lock down $Staging (exit $LASTEXITCODE)" }
    return "$Staging ready (owner $((Get-Acl -LiteralPath $Staging).Owner), ACL = SYSTEM + Administrators)"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER.  Installs each staged file in turn and
#  returns one result object per file.  Self contained on purpose.
#  Guards, in order: nothing else servicing the box, no pending reboot,
#  the staged file still has the hash we copied, the file is Microsoft
#  signed.  Only then expand + DISM.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
$script:RemoteInstallScript = {
    param([string[]]$RemoteFiles, [string[]]$ExpectedHashes, [bool]$Cleanup, [bool]$RequireSignature, [string]$Operator)
    $results = @()

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $RemoteFiles.Count; $i++) {
        $file = $RemoteFiles[$i]
        $expectedHash = ''
        if ($ExpectedHashes.Count -gt $i) { $expectedHash = $ExpectedHashes[$i] }
        $kb = 'KB?'
        if ($file -match '(?i)(KB\d{6,7})') { $kb = $Matches[1].ToUpper() }
        # Work folder/log names: KB + 6 chars from the file name, so two files with one KB never collide.
        $nameHash = [System.BitConverter]::ToString([System.Security.Cryptography.MD5]::Create().ComputeHash([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes((Split-Path -Path $file -Leaf).ToLower()))).Replace('-', '').Substring(0, 6)
        $tag = "$kb-$nameHash"
        $r = [ordered]@{
            Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; KB = $kb; File = (Split-Path -Path $file -Leaf)
            Success = $false; RebootRequired = $false; ExitCode = $null; Message = ''; Detail = @(); Packages = @()
        }
        $extract = $null
        $logPath = $null
        $stage = Split-Path -Path $file -Parent
        try {
            # --- Guard 1: is something else servicing this box right now?  dism/wusa = yes; TiWorker only
            #     when it is actually burning CPU (it idles for minutes after routine maintenance); and the
            #     Windows Update agent is asked directly.  Same block as in RemoteStatusScript.
            $busy = @(Get-Process -Name dism, wusa -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.ProcessName } | Sort-Object -Unique)
            $ti = @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
            if ($ti.Count -gt 0) {
                $cpu1 = 0.0; foreach ($p in $ti) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu1 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
                Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
                $cpu2 = 0.0; foreach ($p in @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu2 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
                if (($cpu2 - $cpu1) -ge 0.25) { $busy += ('TiWorker busy ({0:N1} s CPU in 2 s)' -f ($cpu2 - $cpu1)) }
            }
            try { if ((New-Object -ComObject 'Microsoft.Update.Session').CreateUpdateInstaller().IsBusy) { $busy += 'Windows Update agent installing' } } catch { }
            if ($busy.Count -gt 0) { throw "servicing already running on the server ($($busy -join ', ')) - try again in a few minutes" }
            # --- Guard 2: pending reboot (same hard keys as the status check)
            $cbs = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing'
            $pending = @()
            foreach ($k in 'RebootPending', 'PackagesPending', 'RebootInProgress') { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath "$cbs\$k") { $pending += "CBS:$k" } }
            foreach ($k in 'RebootRequired', 'PostRebootReporting') { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\$k") { $pending += "WU:$k" } }
            if ($pending.Count -gt 0) { throw "pending reboot on the server ($($pending -join ', ')) - reboot first" }
            # --- Guard 3: the staged file is intact (closes the gap between the copy and the install)
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file)) { throw "Staged file not found: $file" }
            if ($expectedHash) {
                $actual = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
                if ($actual -ne $expectedHash) { throw "staged file hash changed since the copy ($actual vs $expectedHash) - refusing to install" }
            }
            # --- Guard 4: Microsoft signature
            if ($RequireSignature) {
                $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature -LiteralPath $file
                $subject = ''
                if ($sig.SignerCertificate) { $subject = $sig.SignerCertificate.Subject }
                if ($sig.Status -ne 'Valid' -or $subject -notmatch 'O=Microsoft Corporation') { throw "signature check failed: status $($sig.Status), signer '$subject'" }
                $r.Detail += "Authenticode: $($sig.Status), $subject"
            }

            $logPath = "$stage\dism-$tag.log"
            $packages = @()
            if ($file.ToLower().EndsWith('.msu')) {
                # Step A: unpack the .msu (a container holding one or more .cab files)
                $extract = "$stage\extract-$tag"
                if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $extract) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $extract -Recurse -Force }
                New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $extract -Force | Out-Null
                $r.Detail += "expand.exe -F:* `"$file`" `"$extract`""
                $null = & expand.exe -F:* "$file" "$extract" 2>&1
                if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "expand.exe failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
                # WSUSSCAN.cab is only metadata; a separate SSU (servicing stack) cab must go first.
                $cabs = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $extract -Filter '*.cab' | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch '^WSUSSCAN' })
                $packages = @($cabs | Sort-Object @{ Expression = { if ($_.Name -match 'SSU') { 0 } else { 1 } } }, Name | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName })
                if ($packages.Count -eq 0) { throw 'No .cab file found inside the .msu' }
            } else {
                $packages = @($file)
            }

            # Step B: DISM installs each package in turn.  /NoRestart = we decide when to reboot.
            foreach ($pkg in $packages) {
                $pkgName = Split-Path -Path $pkg -Leaf
                $r.Detail += "dism.exe /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:`"$pkg`" /NoRestart /Quiet /LogPath:`"$logPath`""
                $null = & dism.exe /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:"$pkg" /NoRestart /Quiet /LogPath:"$logPath" 2>&1
                $code = $LASTEXITCODE
                $hex = '0x{0:X8}' -f ($code -band 0xFFFFFFFF)
                $r.ExitCode = $code
                $r.Packages += "$pkgName -> exit $code ($hex)"
                switch ($hex) {
                    '0x00000000' { }
                    '0x00000BC2' { $r.RebootRequired = $true }
                    '0x800F081E' { throw "$pkgName - DISM 0x800F081E NOT APPLICABLE to this server: wrong Windows build or a missing prerequisite" }
                    '0x800F0922' { throw "$pkgName - DISM 0x800F0922 install failed. Usual causes: pending reboot, missing servicing stack update, System Reserved partition full. See $logPath" }
                    '0x80070002' { throw "$pkgName - DISM 0x80070002 file not found (was the copy complete?)" }
                    default      { throw "$pkgName - DISM returned $code ($hex). See $logPath on the server" }
                }
            }
            $r.Success = $true
            $r.Message = 'Installed'
            if ($r.RebootRequired) { $r.Message = 'Installed - reboot required (3010)' }
            if ($packages.Count -gt 1) { $r.Message += " ($($packages.Count) packages: " + (($packages | ForEach-Object { Split-Path -Path $_ -Leaf }) -join ', ') + ')' }
        } catch {
            $r.Success = $false
            $r.Message = $_.Exception.Message
            if ($r.Packages.Count -gt 0) { $r.Message = "PARTIAL - earlier packages went in: " + ($r.Packages -join '; ') + " - then: " + $r.Message }
            # Pull the interesting lines out of the DISM log so the operator does not have to go looking.
            if ($logPath -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $logPath)) {
                $r.Detail += @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $logPath -Tail 60 | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Error|Failed|0x8' } | Select-Object -Last 8)
            }
        }

        # Step C: leave a result file on the server (survives a lost connection) and an event log entry.
        $resultPath = "$stage\result-$tag.txt"
        try {
            @("Computer=$env:COMPUTERNAME", "KB=$kb", "File=$($r.File)", "Operator=$Operator", "When=$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')",
              "Success=$($r.Success)", "RebootRequired=$($r.RebootRequired)", "ExitCode=$($r.ExitCode)", "Message=$($r.Message)") + @($r.Packages | ForEach-Object { "Package=$_" }) | Set-Content -LiteralPath $resultPath
        } catch { }
        try {
            if (-not [System.Diagnostics.EventLog]::SourceExists('OfflinePatcher')) { New-EventLog -LogName Application -Source 'OfflinePatcher' -ErrorAction Stop }
            $type = 'Information'
            if (-not $r.Success) { $type = 'Error' }
            Write-EventLog -LogName Application -Source 'OfflinePatcher' -EventId 900 -EntryType $type -Message ("Offline Patcher: {0} on {1} by {2} -> {3} (exit {4})" -f $kb, $env:COMPUTERNAME, $Operator, $r.Message, $r.ExitCode) -ErrorAction Stop
        } catch { $r.Detail += "event log entry not written: $($_.Exception.Message)" }

        # Step D: tidy up (only after success - on failure everything stays for investigation)
        if ($Cleanup -and $r.Success) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            if ($extract) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $extract -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
        }
        $results += [pscustomobject]$r
    }
    return $results
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER while DISM is busy: a progress snapshot.
#  The DISM log goes quiet after "CBS session options=0x100!" for the whole
#  install; the real progress is written to C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log as
#  "Progress: UI message updated ... Stage: 1 out of 1. Percent progress: 37."
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
$script:RemoteProgressScript = {
    param([string]$Staging)
    $dism = @(Get-Process -Name dism -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $ti   = @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $tiCpu = 0
    if ($ti.Count -gt 0) { $tiCpu = [int]($ti | Measure-Object -Property CPU -Sum).Sum }

    $pct = ''; $stage = ''; $pctTime = ''
    $cbs = Join-Path $env:windir 'Logs\CBS\CBS.log'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cbs) {
        $line = Get-Content -LiteralPath $cbs -Tail 3000 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Percent progress: \d+' } | Select-Object -Last 1
        if ($line -match '^(\S+ \S+?),.*Stage: (\d+ out of \d+)\. Percent progress: (\d+)') { $pctTime = $Matches[1]; $stage = $Matches[2]; $pct = $Matches[3] }
    }

    $lastDism = ''
    $log = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Staging -Filter 'dism-*.log' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime | Select-Object -Last 1
    if ($log) {
        $l = [string](Get-Content -LiteralPath $log.FullName -Tail 1 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
        if ($l -match '^(\S+ \S+?),.*TID=\d+ (.*?) - \w+::') { $lastDism = '{0} {1}' -f $Matches[1], $Matches[2] } else { $lastDism = $l }
        if ($lastDism.Length -gt 140) { $lastDism = $lastDism.Substring(0, 140) + '...' }
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; DismRunning = ($dism.Count -gt 0); TiWorkerCpuSec = $tiCpu
        Percent = $pct; Stage = $stage; PercentTime = $pctTime; LastDism = $lastDism
    }
}

function Get-InstallProgress {
    # One progress snapshot per server (RemoteProgressScript), all servers asked at once.
    param([string[]]$ComputerName)
    try {
        $conn = Get-ConnectionArgs
        $job = Invoke-Command -ComputerName $ComputerName @conn -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteProgressScript -ArgumentList $script:Config.RemoteStaging -AsJob -ErrorAction Stop
        Wait-PatcherJob -Job $job -Activity 'Reading install progress' -TimeoutSec 60
        $rows = @(Receive-Job -Job $job -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
        Remove-Job -Job $job -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        return $rows
    } catch {
        Write-PatchLog "Progress check failed (the install itself is unaffected): $(Get-ShortError $_)" 'WARN'
        return @()
    }
}

function Write-InstallProgress {
    # What DISM/CBS is up to right now.  With a GROUP of servers this is ONE summary line per poll;
    # a line per server only every ProgressDetailEveryMin (or always when 3 servers or fewer).
    param([string[]]$ComputerName, [int]$ElapsedSec, [switch]$Detail)
    $rows = @(Get-InstallProgress -ComputerName $ComputerName)
    Write-ProgressSummary -Rows $rows -ElapsedSec $ElapsedSec -Detail:$Detail
}

function Write-ProgressSummary {
    # The formatting half, separated so it can be tested without servers.
    param([object[]]$Rows, [int]$ElapsedSec, [switch]$Detail)
    if (-not $Rows -or $Rows.Count -eq 0) { return }
    $min = [int]($ElapsedSec / 60)
    $known = @($Rows | Where-Object { $null -ne $_.Percent -and $_.Percent -ne '' } | ForEach-Object { [int]$_.Percent })
    $alive = @($Rows | Where-Object { $_.DismRunning }).Count
    if ($Rows.Count -gt 1) {
        $summary = '{0} min elapsed - {1} servers installing, dism.exe alive on {2}: ' -f $min, $Rows.Count, $alive
        if ($known.Count -gt 0) {
            $stats = $known | Measure-Object -Minimum -Maximum -Average
            $summary += ('CBS progress {0}%..{1}% (avg {2}%) on {3} of them' -f $stats.Minimum, $stats.Maximum, [int]$stats.Average, $known.Count)
        } else { $summary += 'no CBS progress line yet' }
        Write-PatchLog $summary 'INFO'
    }
    if ($Detail -or $Rows.Count -le 3) {
        foreach ($r in $Rows) {
            $pctText = 'no CBS progress line yet'
            if ($null -ne $r.Percent -and $r.Percent -ne '') { $pctText = "CBS stage $($r.Stage) at $($r.Percent)% (as of $($r.PercentTime))" }
            $dismText = 'dism.exe running'
            if (-not $r.DismRunning) { $dismText = 'dism.exe not running (between packages or finishing)' }
            $name = $r.PSComputerName
            if (-not $name) { $name = $r.Computer }
