            Write-PatchLog ("  {0}: {1} min - {2}, {3}, TiWorker CPU {4} s, last DISM line: {5}" -f $name, $min, $pctText, $dismText, $r.TiWorkerCpuSec, $r.LastDism) 'INFO'
        }
    }
    if ($known.Count -gt 0) { Set-GuiProgress -Percent ([int](($known | Measure-Object -Average).Average)) }
}

function Show-PatcherMessage {
    # One place for every pop-up, so they all look the same and sit on top of the GUI.
    # RETURNS the button pressed ('OK', 'Cancel', 'Yes', 'No').  Capture it, or write  $null = Show-PatcherMessage ...
    param(
        [string]$Text,
        [string]$Title = 'Offline Patcher',
        [string]$Buttons = 'OK',          # OK, OKCancel, YesNo
        [string]$Icon = 'Information',    # Information, Warning, Error, Question
        [string]$Default = 'Button1'      # Button1 / Button2 - which button Enter selects
    )
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
    $lineCount = @($Text -split "`r?`n").Count
    if ($lineCount -gt 22) { return (Show-PatcherLongMessage -Text $Text -Title $Title -Buttons $Buttons -Default $Default) }
    $owner = $script:Gui['Form']
    if ($owner -and -not $owner.IsDisposed) {
        return [string][System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show($owner, $Text, $Title, $Buttons, $Icon, $Default)
    }
    return [string][System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show($Text, $Title, $Buttons, $Icon, $Default)
}

function Show-PatcherLongMessage {
    # A MessageBox taller than the screen loses its buttons; long texts get a scrollable window instead.
    param([string]$Text, [string]$Title, [string]$Buttons = 'OK', [string]$Default = 'Button1')
    $dlg = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Form
    $dlg.Text = $Title; $dlg.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(900, 600); $dlg.StartPosition = 'CenterParent'
    $dlg.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 9); $dlg.MinimizeBox = $false; $dlg.MaximizeBox = $false
    $box = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.TextBox
    $box.Multiline = $true; $box.ReadOnly = $true; $box.ScrollBars = 'Both'; $box.WordWrap = $false; $box.Dock = 'Fill'
    $box.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Consolas', 9); $box.BackColor = 'White'; $box.Text = $Text
    $bottom = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel; $bottom.Dock = 'Bottom'; $bottom.Height = 44
    $labels = @('OK')
    if ($Buttons -eq 'OKCancel') { $labels = @('OK', 'Cancel') }
    if ($Buttons -eq 'YesNo') { $labels = @('Yes', 'No') }
    $x = 880 - (110 * $labels.Count)
    $buttonObjects = @()
    foreach ($label in $labels) {
        $b = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Button
        $b.Text = $label; $b.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(100, 30); $b.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point($x, 7); $b.Anchor = 'Top,Right'
        $b.Tag = $label
        $b.Add_Click({ $dlg.Tag = $this.Tag; $dlg.Close() })
        $bottom.Controls.Add($b); $buttonObjects += $b; $x += 110
    }
    $dlg.Controls.Add($box); $dlg.Controls.Add($bottom); $box.BringToFront(); $box.Select(0, 0)
    # Default button: Button2 = the second (No / Cancel) so Enter can never approve by accident.
    $dlg.AcceptButton = $buttonObjects[0]
    if ($Default -eq 'Button2' -and $buttonObjects.Count -gt 1) { $dlg.AcceptButton = $buttonObjects[1] }
    $dlg.CancelButton = $buttonObjects[-1]
    $dlg.Tag = $labels[-1]   # closing with X = the "safe" answer (No / Cancel / OK)
    $owner = $script:Gui['Form']
    if ($owner -and -not $owner.IsDisposed) { [void]$dlg.ShowDialog($owner) } else { [void]$dlg.ShowDialog() }
    $answer = [string]$dlg.Tag
    $dlg.Dispose()
    return $answer
}

function Confirm-SafetyChecks {
    # THE TWO MANDATORY POP-UPS.  Both must be answered Yes or nothing is installed.
    # The default button is "No" so a stray Enter key can never approve patching.
    # Returns a single [bool]; every other pop-up result is discarded with $null = ...
    param([string[]]$Servers)
    $list = ($Servers -join "`n")
    $who = Get-OperatorIdentity

    Write-PatchLog 'Safety check 1 of 2: asking operator to confirm VMware snapshot' 'WHY'
    $q1 = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'SAFETY CHECK 1 of 2 - VMware snapshot' -Buttons 'YesNo' -Icon 'Warning' -Default 'Button2' -Text @"
Has a VMware SNAPSHOT been taken of every server below?

$list

Answer No and nothing will be installed.
"@
    if ($q1 -ne 'Yes') {
        Write-PatchLog "ABORTED - $who did not confirm the VMware snapshot (answer: $q1)" 'ERROR'
        $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Patching aborted. Take the snapshots first, then come back.' -Title 'Aborted' -Icon 'Error'
        return [bool]$false
    }
    Write-PatchLog "Confirmed by ${who}: VMware snapshot taken for $($Servers -join ', ')" 'OK'

    Write-PatchLog 'Safety check 2 of 2: asking operator to confirm Trellix maintenance mode' 'WHY'
    $q2 = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'SAFETY CHECK 2 of 2 - Trellix' -Buttons 'YesNo' -Icon 'Warning' -Default 'Button2' -Text @"
Has TRELLIX been placed into MAINTENANCE MODE for every server below?

$list

Answer No and nothing will be installed.
"@
    if ($q2 -ne 'Yes') {
        Write-PatchLog "ABORTED - $who did not confirm Trellix maintenance mode (answer: $q2)" 'ERROR'
        $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Patching aborted. Put Trellix into maintenance mode first, then come back.' -Title 'Aborted' -Icon 'Error'
        return [bool]$false
    }
    Write-PatchLog "Confirmed by ${who}: Trellix in maintenance mode for $($Servers -join ', ')" 'OK'
    return [bool]$true
}

function New-PatchPlan {
    # One row per (server, patch) with Go = $true/$false and the reason.  The decision itself
    # lives in Get-PatchVerdict (04-Patches.ps1) so the grid and the plan can never disagree.
    param([string[]]$ComputerName, [object[]]$Patches)
    $plan = @()
    foreach ($c in $ComputerName) {
        $s = $script:ServerStatus[$c]
        foreach ($p in $Patches) {
            $v = Get-PatchVerdict -Status $s -Patch $p
            $plan += [pscustomobject]@{ Computer = $c; KB = $p.KB; Name = $p.Name; File = $p.FullName; Hash = $p.Hash; Go = $v.Go; Reason = $v.Reason }
        }
    }
    return $plan
}

function Install-PatchOnServers {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$ComputerName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][object[]]$Patches      # objects from Get-PatchFiles
    )
    $targets = @(Get-UniqueNames $ComputerName)
    $who = Get-OperatorIdentity
    Write-PatchLog ("=== INSTALL REQUESTED by {0}: {1} on {2} ===" -f $who, (($Patches | ForEach-Object { $_.KB }) -join ', '), ($targets -join ', ')) 'INFO'

    # 1. Fresh status, 2. plan
    Write-PatchLog 'Pre-flight: refreshing status so we never patch a server that is pending a reboot or busy' 'WHY'
    Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $targets | Out-Null
    $targets = @(Remove-DuplicateServers $targets)
    $plan = New-PatchPlan -ComputerName $targets -Patches $Patches
    foreach ($item in $plan) {
        $lvl = 'WARN'; if ($item.Go) { $lvl = 'INFO' }
        Write-PatchLog ("Plan: {0}  {1}  -> {2}" -f $item.Computer, $item.KB, $item.Reason) $lvl
    }
    $todo = @($plan | Where-Object { $_.Go })
    if ($todo.Count -eq 0) {
        $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text "Nothing to install - every server/patch pair is either done, blocked or unreachable. See the log for the reason per server." -Title 'Nothing to do' -Icon 'Information'
        return @()
    }

    # 3. Show the plan
    $planText = ($plan | ForEach-Object { '{0,-36} {1,-10} {2}' -f $_.Computer, $_.KB, $_.Reason }) -join "`n"
    $ok = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'The plan' -Buttons 'OKCancel' -Icon 'Question' -Text @"
This is what will happen ("ready" rows are installed, the rest are skipped):

$planText

Continue to the safety checks?
"@
    if ($ok -ne 'OK') { Write-PatchLog "$who cancelled at the plan screen" 'WARN'; return @() }

    # 4 + 5. The two mandatory safety pop-ups.  Strict comparison: anything but a real $true aborts.
    $goServers = @(Get-UniqueNames ($todo | ForEach-Object { $_.Computer }))
    $confirmed = Confirm-SafetyChecks -Servers $goServers
    if ($confirmed -isnot [bool] -or $confirmed -ne $true) { Write-PatchLog 'Safety checks not confirmed - nothing was touched' 'WARN'; return @() }

    # 6a. The pop-ups may have been open for a long time: check the servers AGAIN and drop any that changed.
    Write-PatchLog 'Re-checking the servers now that the safety checks are done (status may be minutes old)' 'WHY'
    Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $goServers | Out-Null
    $recheck = New-PatchPlan -ComputerName $goServers -Patches $Patches
    $stillGo = @()
    foreach ($item in $todo) {
        $now = $recheck | Where-Object { $_.Computer -eq $item.Computer -and $_.KB -eq $item.KB } | Select-Object -First 1
        if ($now -and $now.Go) { $stillGo += $item } else { Write-PatchLog ("Dropped {0} {1} - no longer ready: {2}" -f $item.Computer, $item.KB, $now.Reason) 'WARN' }
    }
    $todo = $stillGo
    $goServers = @(Get-UniqueNames ($todo | ForEach-Object { $_.Computer }))
    if ($todo.Count -eq 0) {
        $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Every server changed state while the pop-ups were open (pending reboot, busy or unreachable). Nothing was installed - check the log and try again.' -Title 'Nothing to do' -Icon 'Warning'
        return @()
    }

    # 6b + 7. Per server: session, locked staging folder, copy - and the install is started the moment
    #         that server's copy is verified, so server 1 is already installing while server 2 copies.
    #         Copies go one server at a time (the log stays readable); installs run in parallel.
    #         Everything sits in try/finally so sessions never leak.
    $sessions = @()
    $filesByComputer = @{}
    $results = @()
    $jobs = @()
    $keepOpen = @()     # sessions whose install is still running on the server (timeout) - never torn down
    $script:EnvelopeTipShown = $false
    try {
        $n = 0
        foreach ($c in $goServers) {
            $n++
            $sess = $null
            try {
                $conn = Get-ConnectionArgs
                Write-PatchLog ("[{0}/{1}] New-PSSession -ComputerName {2} -Port {3}" -f $n, $goServers.Count, $c, $conn.Port) 'CMD'
                $sess = New-PSSession -ComputerName $c @conn -ErrorAction Stop
                $ready = Invoke-Command -Session $sess -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteStagingScript -ArgumentList $script:Config.RemoteStaging -ErrorAction Stop
                Write-PatchLog "$c - $ready" 'INFO'

                $remoteFiles = @()
                $remoteHashes = @()
                foreach ($item in @($todo | Where-Object { $_.Computer -eq $c })) {
                    # Built as a string on purpose: Join-Path would check the drive letter on THIS machine.
                    $dest = $script:Config.RemoteStaging.TrimEnd('\') + '\' + $item.Name
                    $sizeMB = [math]::Round((Get-Item -LiteralPath $item.File).Length / 1MB, 1)
                    Write-PatchLog ("Copy-FileToSession -Path '{0}' -Destination '{1}' -Session [{2}]   ({3} MB, sent in WinRM-sized slices - this takes a while)" -f $item.File, $dest, $c, $sizeMB) 'CMD'
                    Copy-FileToSession -Path $item.File -Destination $dest -Session $sess -LocalHash $item.Hash | Out-Null
                    $remoteFiles += $dest
                    $remoteHashes += $item.Hash
                }
                $filesByComputer[$c] = $remoteFiles
                $sessions += $sess
                Write-PatchLog ("Invoke-Command -Session [{0}] -AsJob  (install script: {1})" -f $c, ($remoteFiles -join ', ')) 'CMD'
                $jobs += Invoke-Command -Session $sess -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteInstallScript -ArgumentList $remoteFiles, $remoteHashes, $script:Config.CleanupStaging, $script:Config.RequireValidSignature, $who -AsJob
                Write-PatchLog "$c - install started on the server; it keeps running while the next server is copied" 'OK'
            } catch {
                $msg = Get-ShortError $_
                Write-PatchLog "$c - staging failed: $msg" 'ERROR'
                Write-PatchLog "   failed at: $(Get-ErrorLocation $_)" 'WHY'
                if ($sess) { Remove-PSSession -Session $sess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
                foreach ($item in @($todo | Where-Object { $_.Computer -eq $c })) {
                    $results += New-InstallResult -Computer $c -KB $item.KB -File $item.Name -Message "staging failed: $msg"
                }
            }
        }

        # 8. Wait for every install, keeping the GUI alive and reporting progress, then collect.
        if ($jobs.Count -gt 0) {
            Write-PatchLog ("All copies done; DISM is running on {0} server(s). Its log goes quiet after 'CBS session options'; real progress comes from CBS.log: a summary line every {1} s, one line per server every {2} min. A cumulative update usually takes 10-30 min - leave this window open (status checks still work meanwhile)." -f $jobs.Count, $script:Config.ProgressEverySec, $script:Config.ProgressDetailEveryMin) 'WHY'
        }
        $finished = @('Completed', 'Failed', 'Stopped', 'Disconnected')
        $watch = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
        $lastProgress = 0
        $lastDetail = 0
        while (@($jobs | Where-Object { $finished -notcontains $_.State }).Count -gt 0 -and $watch.Elapsed.TotalMinutes -lt $script:Config.InstallTimeoutMin) {
            $running = @($jobs | Where-Object { $finished -notcontains $_.State } | ForEach-Object { $_.Location })
            Set-GuiStatus ('Installing on {0} server(s) [{1}] ... {2} min {3} s (DISM is slow, grab a coffee)' -f $running.Count, ($running -join ', '), [int][math]::Floor($watch.Elapsed.TotalMinutes), $watch.Elapsed.Seconds)
            if ($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds - $lastProgress -ge $script:Config.ProgressEverySec) {
                $lastProgress = $watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds
                $detail = $false
                if ($watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds - $lastDetail -ge ($script:Config.ProgressDetailEveryMin * 60)) { $detail = $true; $lastDetail = $watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds }
                Write-InstallProgress -ComputerName $running -ElapsedSec ([int]$watch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds) -Detail:$detail
            }
            Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
        }
        foreach ($j in $jobs) {
            $c = $j.Location
            if ($finished -notcontains $j.State -or $j.State -eq 'Disconnected') {
                # Still running after the timeout (or the connection dropped).  Do NOT stop the job and do
                # NOT close the session: that would kill DISM half way.  Disconnect so the server carries on.
                $sess = $sessions | Where-Object { $_.ComputerName -eq $c } | Select-Object -First 1
                $keepOpen += $sess
                try { Disconnect-PSSession -Session $sess -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null } catch { }
                $msg = "UNKNOWN - still running on the server after $($script:Config.InstallTimeoutMin) min (state $($j.State)). The install continues there. Result file: $($script:Config.RemoteStaging)\result-*.txt on $c. Reconnect: Get-PSSession -ComputerName $c | Connect-PSSession"
                Write-PatchLog "$c - $msg" 'ERROR'
                foreach ($f in $filesByComputer[$c]) { $results += New-InstallResult -Computer $c -KB (Get-KBFromName $f) -File (Split-Path -Path $f -Leaf) -Message $msg }
                continue
            }
            $jobErrors = @()
            $out = @(Receive-Job -Job $j -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -ErrorVariable jobErrors)
            if ($out.Count -eq 0) {
                $reason = 'no result returned'
                if ($jobErrors.Count -gt 0) { $reason = Get-ShortError $jobErrors[0] }
                Write-PatchLog "$c - install job failed: $reason" 'ERROR'
                foreach ($f in $filesByComputer[$c]) { $results += New-InstallResult -Computer $c -KB (Get-KBFromName $f) -File (Split-Path -Path $f -Leaf) -Message $reason }
            }
            foreach ($r in $out) {
                $lvl = 'ERROR'; if ($r.Success) { $lvl = 'OK' }
                Write-PatchLog ("RESULT {0}  {1}  exit {2}  -> {3}   (by {4})" -f $r.Computer, $r.KB, $r.ExitCode, $r.Message, $who) $lvl
                foreach ($d in $r.Detail) { Write-PatchLog "    $d" 'CMD' }
                $results += $r
            }
            Remove-Job -Job $j -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    } finally {
        foreach ($sess in $sessions) {
            if ($keepOpen -contains $sess) { continue }
            Remove-PSSession -Session $sess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    }

    # 9. Fresh status again so the grid tells the truth
    Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $goServers | Out-Null
    $good = @($results | Where-Object { $_.Success }).Count
    $bad  = @($results | Where-Object { -not $_.Success }).Count
    $reb  = @($results | Where-Object { $_.RebootRequired }).Count
    Write-PatchLog ("=== INSTALL FINISHED (by {3}): {0} ok, {1} failed/unknown, {2} need a reboot ===" -f $good, $bad, $reb, $who) 'INFO'
    return $results
}

function New-InstallResult {
    # A failure result shaped exactly like the ones the remote script returns.
    param([string]$Computer, [string]$KB, [string]$File, [string]$Message)
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Computer = $Computer; KB = $KB; File = $File; Success = $false; RebootRequired = $false; ExitCode = $null; Message = $Message; Detail = @(); Packages = @() }
}

function Get-KBFromName {
    param([string]$Name)
    if ($Name -match '(?i)(KB\d{6,7})') { return $Matches[1].ToUpper() }
    return 'KB?'
}

function Remove-DuplicateServers {
    # Two names that resolve to the SAME computer (short name + FQDN, or different case) would get two
    # concurrent installs.  After a status check we know each server's real name, so keep the first alias.
    param([string[]]$Names)
    $seen = @{}
    $keep = @()
    foreach ($n in $Names) {
        $s = $script:ServerStatus[$n]
        $real = $n
        if ($s -and $s.Reachable -and $s.Computer) { $real = $s.Computer.ToUpper() }
        if ($seen.ContainsKey($real)) {
            Write-PatchLog "$n is the same computer as $($seen[$real]) ($real) - skipping the duplicate" 'WARN'
            continue
        }
        $seen[$real] = $n
        $keep += $n
    }
    return $keep
}

# RUNS ON THE TARGET SERVER: refuses to reboot while servicing is active, then schedules the
# restart 10 s out with shutdown.exe so this call returns before the connection is cut.
$script:RemoteRebootScript = {
    param([string]$Operator)
    # Same "really servicing?" test as the status and install scripts: dism/wusa present, TiWorker actually
    # busy (CPU over 2 s), or the Windows Update agent installing.  An idle TiWorker does not block a reboot.
    $busy = @(Get-Process -Name dism, wusa -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.ProcessName } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $ti = @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    if ($ti.Count -gt 0) {
        $cpu1 = 0.0; foreach ($p in $ti) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu1 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
        $cpu2 = 0.0; foreach ($p in @(Get-Process -Name TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { try { if ($p.CPU) { $cpu2 += $p.CPU } } catch { } }
        if (($cpu2 - $cpu1) -ge 0.25) { $busy += ('TiWorker busy ({0:N1} s CPU in 2 s)' -f ($cpu2 - $cpu1)) }
    }
    try { if ((New-Object -ComObject 'Microsoft.Update.Session').CreateUpdateInstaller().IsBusy) { $busy += 'Windows Update agent installing' } } catch { }
    if ($busy.Count -gt 0) { throw "servicing still running ($($busy -join ', ')) - NOT rebooting; try again in a few minutes" }
    $null = & shutdown.exe /r /t 10 /d p:2:17 /c "Offline Patcher reboot requested by $Operator" 2>&1
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "shutdown.exe returned $LASTEXITCODE" }
    return "reboot scheduled in 10 s on $env:COMPUTERNAME"
}

function Restart-PatchedServers {
    # Reboots over WinRM.  Separate button, separate confirmations, never automatic.
    # Default set = servers whose FRESH status says "pending reboot".  Anything else needs a second,
    # explicit Yes.  On the server, a reboot is refused while dism/TiWorker are still running.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$ComputerName)
    $targets = @(Get-UniqueNames $ComputerName)
    $who = Get-OperatorIdentity
    Write-PatchLog "Reboot requested by $who for $($targets -join ', ') - checking status first" 'WHY'
    Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $targets | Out-Null
    $targets = @(Remove-DuplicateServers $targets)
    $pending = @(); $notPending = @(); $unreachable = @()
    foreach ($c in $targets) {
        $s = $script:ServerStatus[$c]
        if (-not $s -or -not $s.Reachable) { $unreachable += $c }
        elseif ($s.PendingReboot) { $pending += $c }
        else { $notPending += $c }
    }
    foreach ($c in $unreachable) { Write-PatchLog "$c - unreachable, not rebooting" 'WARN' }

    $toReboot = @()
    if ($pending.Count -gt 0) {
        $a = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'Reboot?' -Buttons 'YesNo' -Icon 'Warning' -Default 'Button2' -Text ("These servers are PENDING A REBOOT. Reboot them now?`n`n{0}" -f ($pending -join "`n"))
        if ($a -eq 'Yes') { $toReboot += $pending } else { Write-PatchLog "$who answered $a - pending servers not rebooted" 'WARN' }
    }
    if ($notPending.Count -gt 0) {
        $a = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'Reboot servers that are NOT pending a reboot?' -Buttons 'YesNo' -Icon 'Warning' -Default 'Button2' -Text ("These servers do NOT need a reboot according to their status. Reboot them anyway?`n`n{0}`n`n(Logged-on users will be disconnected.)" -f ($notPending -join "`n"))
        if ($a -eq 'Yes') { $toReboot += $notPending } else { Write-PatchLog "$who answered $a - servers not pending a reboot are left alone" 'INFO' }
    }
    if ($toReboot.Count -eq 0) { Write-PatchLog 'No reboot sent' 'INFO'; return }

    foreach ($c in $toReboot) {
        try {
            $conn = Get-ConnectionArgs
            Write-PatchLog "Invoke-Command -ComputerName $c -Port $($conn.Port) (RemoteRebootScript: refuse if dism/TiWorker busy, then shutdown.exe /r /t 10)" 'CMD'
            $msg = Invoke-Command -ComputerName $c @conn -ScriptBlock $script:RemoteRebootScript -ArgumentList $who -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-PatchLog "REBOOT $c - $msg (by $who)" 'OK'
            $script:ServerStatus.Remove($c)   # old status is now meaningless
        } catch {
            $err = Get-ShortError $_
            if ($err -match 'shut down|restart|connection|closed|aborted') { Write-PatchLog "REBOOT $c - the connection dropped while the reboot was being sent; it is probably rebooting: $err" 'WARN'; $script:ServerStatus.Remove($c) }
            else { Write-PatchLog "REBOOT $c - refused or failed: $err" 'ERROR' }
        }
    }
}
# ===================== END 06-Install.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 07-Gui.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  07-Gui.ps1  -  THE PATCH PALACE (Windows Forms, built in PowerShell)
#  The operator's name in the title, banner and quips comes from $Config.OperatorName.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Layout of the main tab:
#    [ banner: title + random quip ]
#    [ toolbar: group picker, reload, check status, tick/untick, creds, log ]
#    [ server grid (left, fills) ............ | patch list + big buttons (right) ]
#    [ live log (bottom)                                                        ]
#    [ status bar + patch-o-meter ]
#  Second tab = "Code Tour": click a topic, read the explanation AND the live
#  source code of the function that is running right now.
#
#  Every button calls Invoke-GuiAction, which disables the buttons, runs the
#  work, catches errors into the log, then re-enables everything.  Nothing in
#  this file talks to a server directly - it only calls the functions in
#  03/04/05/06 so the logic can be tested from the console without a GUI.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  07-Gui.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Fixed here:
#  R-02 results list filtered to real result objects; R-12 grid cells now
#  come from Get-PatchVerdict (same rules as the plan); R-28 window could
#  be closed and the details dialog opened while an install was running
#  (FormClosing guard, double-click guard, group box disabled while
#  busy); R-30 credentials cleared when the GUI closes; R-32 "Open
#  patches" / notepad paths with spaces; every unused pop-up result is
#  discarded with $null = (R-01 rule).
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Checked    : [ ] every button   [ ] closing during an install is refused
#               [ ] compared with CODE-REVIEW.md
#  Comments   :
#    -
# =====================================================================

$script:Quips = @(
    'Snapshots first, heroics later.'
    "Trellix in maintenance mode? Of course you did, $($script:Config.OperatorName)."
    'Patching: like gardening, but the weeds fight back.'
    'Every reboot is a small holiday for a server.'
    'KBs do not install themselves. Well... they do now.'
    'If in doubt, read the log. The log never lies (it just mumbles).'
    'Rule #1: the plan screen is not decorative.'
    '3010 is a happy number. It means "reboot me", not "I failed".'
    'Zero servers pending reboot? Frame it.'
    'Green is good. Yellow is work. Red is coffee.'
    'Port 5985: the little door every server leaves open for you.'
    'Patch Tuesday is a lifestyle.'
)

function Get-RandomQuip { return ($script:Quips | Get-Random) }

function Get-ShortOsName {
    # "Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Standard" -> "2022 Std"
    param([string]$Caption)
    if (-not $Caption) { return '' }
    $year = ''
    if ($Caption -match '(20\d\d)') { $year = $Matches[1] }
    $edition = ''
    if ($Caption -match 'Datacenter') { $edition = 'DC' } elseif ($Caption -match 'Standard') { $edition = 'Std' }
    return ("$year $edition").Trim()
}

function Get-PatchCellText {
    # What to show in a KB column for one server.  The decision is Get-PatchVerdict (04-Patches.ps1),
    # the SAME function the install plan uses, so the grid can never promise what the plan refuses.
    param($Status, $Patch)
    return (Get-PatchVerdict -Status $Status -Patch $Patch).Cell
}

function Get-CheckedServers {
    $names = @()
    foreach ($item in $script:Gui['ServerList'].Items) { if ($item.Checked) { $names += $item.Text } }
    return @(Get-UniqueNames $names)
}

function Get-CheckedPatches {
    $list = $script:Gui['PatchList']
    $picked = @()
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $list.Items.Count; $i++) {
        if ($list.GetItemChecked($i)) { $picked += $script:Patches[$i] }
    }
    return $picked
}

function Update-PatchList {
    $list = $script:Gui['PatchList']
    $list.Items.Clear()
    foreach ($p in $script:Patches) {
        $line = '{0}  ({1} MB, {2}' -f $p.KB, $p.SizeMB, $p.Type
        if ($p.TargetBuild -gt 0) { $line += ', ' + $p.TargetOs } elseif ($p.OsLine) { $line += ', ' + $p.OsLine + ' ?' }
        $line += ')'
        if ($p.Signature -ne 'Valid') { $line += '  UNSIGNED / ' + $p.Signature }
        [void]$list.Items.Add($line, $false)
    }
    $script:Gui['PatchFolderLabel'].Text = 'Folder: ' + $script:Config.PatchFolder
}

function Update-ServerList {
    # Rebuilds the grid from $script:Groups + $script:Patches + $script:ServerStatus.
    $lv = $script:Gui['ServerList']
    $wasChecked = @(Get-CheckedServers)
    $lv.BeginUpdate()
    $lv.Items.Clear()
    $lv.Columns.Clear()
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Server', 170)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Group', 110)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('WinRM', 75)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('OS', 70)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Build', 95)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Pending reboot', 150)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Up (d)', 55)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Free C: GB', 75)
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Newest hotfixes (same day)', 230)
    foreach ($p in $script:Patches) { [void]$lv.Columns.Add($p.KB, 105) }
    [void]$lv.Columns.Add('Checked at', 80)

    $filter = [string]$script:Gui['GroupCombo'].SelectedItem
    foreach ($g in $script:Groups) {
        if ($filter -and $filter -ne '(all groups)' -and $filter -ne $g.Name) { continue }
        foreach ($name in $g.Servers) {
            $s = $script:ServerStatus[$name]
            $item = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ListViewItem($name)
            [void]$item.SubItems.Add($g.Name)
            if (-not $s) {
                foreach ($i in 1..7) { [void]$item.SubItems.Add('') }
                foreach ($p in $script:Patches) { [void]$item.SubItems.Add('not checked') }
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add('')
                $item.BackColor = 'White'
            } elseif (-not $s.Reachable) {
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add('FAILED')
                foreach ($i in 1..6) { [void]$item.SubItems.Add('') }
                foreach ($p in $script:Patches) { [void]$item.SubItems.Add('?') }
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add($s.Checked.ToString('HH:mm:ss'))
                $item.BackColor = 'LightGray'
                $item.ToolTipText = $s.Error
            } else {
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add('OK')
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add((Get-ShortOsName $s.Caption))
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add($s.Build)
                $pend = 'no'
                if ($s.PendingReboot) { $pend = 'YES: ' + $s.RebootReasons } elseif ($s.PfroPresent) { $pend = 'no (PFRO only, ignored)' }
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add($pend)
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add([string]$s.UptimeDays)
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add([string]$s.FreeGB)
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add($s.LastHotFix)
                $anyReady = $false; $allInstalled = ($script:Patches.Count -gt 0)
                foreach ($p in $script:Patches) {
                    $cell = Get-PatchCellText -Status $s -Patch $p
                    [void]$item.SubItems.Add($cell)
                    if ($cell -eq 'READY') { $anyReady = $true }
                    if ($cell -notlike 'Installed*') { $allInstalled = $false }
                }
                [void]$item.SubItems.Add($s.Checked.ToString('HH:mm:ss'))
                if ($s.PendingReboot) { $item.BackColor = 'MistyRose' }
                elseif ($anyReady)    { $item.BackColor = 'LemonChiffon' }
                elseif ($allInstalled) { $item.BackColor = 'Honeydew' }
                else { $item.BackColor = 'White' }
                if ($s.FreeGB -lt $script:Config.WarnFreeGB) { $item.SubItems[7].ForeColor = 'Red'; $item.UseItemStyleForSubItems = $false }
            }
            if ($wasChecked -contains $name) { $item.Checked = $true }
            [void]$lv.Items.Add($item)
        }
    }
    $lv.EndUpdate()
    $script:Gui['CountLabel'].Text = ('{0} server row(s) shown, {1} ticked' -f $lv.Items.Count, (Get-CheckedServers).Count)
}

function Invoke-GuiAction {
    # Wraps every button click: one place for busy-state, error catching and refresh.
    # -ReadOnly actions (status check, WinRM test) may run WHILE an install is in progress - the
    # install's own wait loop pumps the message queue, so a click arrives in the middle of it and the
    # read-only action simply runs nested, without touching the busy flag or the locked buttons.
    param([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Action, [switch]$ReadOnly)
    if ($script:Gui['Busy']) {
        if (-not $ReadOnly) { Write-PatchLog "Still busy with '$($script:Gui['BusyName'])' - wait for it to finish" 'WARN'; return }
        if ($script:Gui['NestedBusy']) { Write-PatchLog "A read-only action is already running alongside '$($script:Gui['BusyName'])' - wait for it" 'WARN'; return }
        $script:Gui['NestedBusy'] = $true
        Write-PatchLog "$Name requested while '$($script:Gui['BusyName'])' is running - allowed, it is read-only" 'WHY'
        try {
            & $Action
        } catch {
            Write-PatchLog "$Name failed: $(Get-ShortError $_)" 'ERROR'
        } finally {
            $script:Gui['NestedBusy'] = $false
            Update-ServerList
        }
        return
    }
    $script:Gui['Busy'] = $true
    $script:Gui['BusyName'] = $Name
    foreach ($b in $script:Gui['Buttons']) { if ($b.Tag -ne 'readonly') { $b.Enabled = $false } }
    $script:Gui['Progress'].Style = 'Marquee'
    Set-GuiStatus "$Name ..."
    try {
        & $Action
    } catch {
        Write-PatchLog "$Name failed: $(Get-ShortError $_)" 'ERROR'
        Write-PatchLog "   failed at: $(Get-ErrorLocation $_)" 'WHY'
    } finally {
        $script:Gui['Progress'].Style = 'Blocks'
        $script:Gui['Progress'].Value = 0
        foreach ($b in $script:Gui['Buttons']) { $b.Enabled = $true }
        $script:Gui['Busy'] = $false
        $script:Gui['QuipLabel'].Text = Get-RandomQuip
        Update-ServerList
        Set-GuiStatus 'Ready.'
    }
}

function Get-ServerDetailsText {
    # Everything we know about one server as plain text: status, patch verdicts, both update lists.
    param([string]$Name)
    $s = $script:ServerStatus[$Name]
    $sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
    $rule = '-' * 110
    [void]$sb.AppendLine("SERVER: $Name   (checked $($s.Checked))")
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($rule)
    foreach ($p in 'Computer', 'Reachable', 'Error', 'Caption', 'Build', 'LastBoot', 'UptimeDays', 'FreeGB', 'PendingReboot', 'RebootReasons', 'PfroPresent', 'ServicingActive', 'ServicingReasons', 'LastHotFix', 'PSVersion') {
        [void]$sb.AppendLine(('{0,-14} : {1}' -f $p, $s.$p))
    }
    [void]$sb.AppendLine()
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  HOW TO READ THIS')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  Build          = the real patch level.  The number after the dot (the UBR) changes with every cumulative')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('                   update; the Microsoft update-history page lists it next to each KB, e.g. "KB5122882 (OS Build 20348.5622)".')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('                   It only moves AFTER the reboot that finishes the install.')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  LastHotFix     = every Get-HotFix entry from the most recent install date.  The cumulative update and the')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('                   .NET cumulative update normally arrive on the same day, so several KBs can share that date.')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  PendingReboot  = true only for the hard signs: CBS RebootPending, CBS PackagesPending, WU RebootRequired.')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  PfroPresent    = PendingFileRenameOperations exists (see below).  Not counted unless you turn it on in 01-Config.ps1.')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  ServicingActive= dism.exe / TiWorker.exe / wusa.exe running right now.  Blocks installs and reboots; TiWorker')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('                   also runs for routine maintenance, so re-check in a minute before worrying.')

    [void]$sb.AppendLine()
    [void]$sb.AppendLine(("PENDING FILE RENAME OPERATIONS  ({0} entries, first {1} shown)" -f $s.PfroCount, @($s.PfroEntries).Count))
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($rule)
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  Files Windows will rename or delete at the next boot because they were locked.  Installers and anti-virus')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  products add to this list constantly and often leave it behind, so on its own it is a weak sign of a')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  needed reboot.  Look at the paths: temp files or AV files = ignore; Windows\WinSxS or servicing files = reboot.')
    if (@($s.PfroEntries).Count -eq 0) { [void]$sb.AppendLine('  (none)') }
    foreach ($line in @($s.PfroEntries)) { [void]$sb.AppendLine("  $line") }

    [void]$sb.AppendLine()
    [void]$sb.AppendLine("PATCHES IN \patches vs THIS SERVER")
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($rule)
    if ($script:Patches.Count -eq 0) { [void]$sb.AppendLine('  (no patch files found)') }
    foreach ($p in $script:Patches) { [void]$sb.AppendLine(('  {0,-10}  {1,-20}  {2}' -f $p.KB, (Get-PatchCellText -Status $s -Patch $p), $p.Name)) }

    [void]$sb.AppendLine()
    [void]$sb.AppendLine(("INSTALLED HOTFIXES - Get-HotFix / Win32_QuickFixEngineering  ({0} entries)" -f @($s.HotFixIDs).Count))
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($rule)
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  Only CBS packages still present on the box.  Each cumulative update supersedes the previous one,')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  which then drops off this list - so a well patched server shows only a handful here.  This is')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  the primary "is KB x installed?" source because it reflects what is on disk right now.')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine(('  {0,-10}  {1,-12}  {2,-24}  {3}' -f 'KB', 'Installed', 'Type', 'Installed by'))
    foreach ($line in @($s.HotFixLines)) { [void]$sb.AppendLine("  $line") }

    [void]$sb.AppendLine()
    [void]$sb.AppendLine(("WINDOWS UPDATE HISTORY - Windows Update Agent, newest first  (showing {0} of {1})" -f @($s.HistoryLines).Count, $s.HistoryCount))
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($rule)
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  The same list as Settings > Update history: every install attempt, including superseded updates,')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  Defender definitions and failures.  A KB whose newest entry is a successful Install counts as')
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('  "Installed (history)" in the grid even when Get-HotFix no longer lists it.')
    if ($s.HistoryError) { [void]$sb.AppendLine("  COULD NOT READ THE HISTORY: $($s.HistoryError)") }
    [void]$sb.AppendLine(('  {0,-16}  {1,-9}  {2,-18}  {3,-10}  {4}' -f 'Date', 'Operation', 'Result', 'KB', 'Title'))
    foreach ($line in @($s.HistoryLines)) { [void]$sb.AppendLine("  $line") }
    return $sb.ToString()
}

function Show-ServerDetails {
    # Double-click on a row: a scrollable, copyable window with everything we know about that server.
    param([string]$Name)
    $s = $script:ServerStatus[$Name]
    if (-not $s) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text "$Name has not been checked yet. Tick it and press 'Check status'." -Title $Name; return }

    $dlg = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Form
    $dlg.Text = "Details: $Name"
    $dlg.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(1100, 720)
    $dlg.StartPosition = 'CenterParent'
    $dlg.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 9)

    $box = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.TextBox
    $box.Multiline = $true; $box.ReadOnly = $true; $box.ScrollBars = 'Both'; $box.WordWrap = $false
    $box.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Consolas', 9); $box.BackColor = 'White'; $box.Dock = 'Fill'
    $box.Text = Get-ServerDetailsText -Name $Name
    $box.Select(0, 0)

    $bottom = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $bottom.Dock = 'Bottom'; $bottom.Height = 40
    $hint = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $hint.Text = 'Ctrl+A then Ctrl+C copies everything.'; $hint.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(10, 12); $hint.AutoSize = $true; $hint.ForeColor = 'DimGray'
    $close = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Button
    $close.Text = 'Close'; $close.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(90, 28); $close.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(980, 6); $close.Anchor = 'Top,Right'
    $close.Add_Click({ $dlg.Close() })
    $bottom.Controls.Add($hint); $bottom.Controls.Add($close)

    $dlg.Controls.Add($box); $dlg.Controls.Add($bottom)
    $box.BringToFront()
    $dlg.CancelButton = $close
    [void]$dlg.ShowDialog($script:Gui['Form'])
    $dlg.Dispose()
}

function New-GuiButton {
    # -ReadOnly buttons stay enabled while an install runs (they only look, never change anything).
    param([string]$Text, [int]$X, [int]$Y, [int]$W = 150, [int]$H = 30, [string]$Colour = '', [scriptblock]$OnClick, [string]$Tip = '', [switch]$ReadOnly)
    $b = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Button
    $b.Text = $Text; $b.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point($X, $Y); $b.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size($W, $H)
    $b.UseVisualStyleBackColor = $true
    if ($Colour) { $b.BackColor = $Colour; $b.UseVisualStyleBackColor = $false }
    if ($Tip) { $script:Gui['Tips'].SetToolTip($b, $Tip) }
    if ($ReadOnly) { $b.Tag = 'readonly' }
    $b.Add_Click($OnClick)
    $script:Gui['Buttons'] += $b
    return $b
}

function Show-PatcherGui {
    param([switch]$NoShow)   # -NoShow builds the form without displaying it (used for self-tests)
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
    [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::EnableVisualStyles()

    $script:Gui = @{ Buttons = @(); Busy = $false; Tips = (New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ToolTip) }
    $font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 9)

    $form = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Form
    $form.Text = "$($script:Config.OperatorName)'s Patch Palace - Offline Server 2022 patching over WinRM"
    $form.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(1300, 860)
    $form.MinimumSize = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(1000, 700)
    $form.StartPosition = 'CenterScreen'
    $form.Font = $font
    $script:Gui['Form'] = $form

    $tabs = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.TabControl
    $tabs.Dock = 'Fill'
    $tabMain = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.TabPage; $tabMain.Text = '  Patch Console  '
    $tabTour = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.TabPage; $tabTour.Text = '  Code Tour - how it works  '
    $tabs.TabPages.AddRange(@($tabMain, $tabTour))

    # ---------------- status bar (added first so it docks at the very bottom) ----------------
    $strip = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.StatusStrip
    $statusLabel = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ToolStripStatusLabel
    $statusLabel.Text = 'Ready.'; $statusLabel.Spring = $true; $statusLabel.TextAlign = 'MiddleLeft'
    $progress = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ToolStripProgressBar
    $progress.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(220, 16); $progress.ToolTipText = 'Patch-o-meter'
    [void]$strip.Items.Add($statusLabel); [void]$strip.Items.Add($progress)
    $script:Gui['StatusLabel'] = $statusLabel; $script:Gui['Progress'] = $progress

    # ================= MAIN TAB =================
    # Fill control first, then the docked edges (WinForms docks the last-added control first).
    $split = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.SplitContainer
    $split.Dock = 'Fill'; $split.Orientation = 'Horizontal'
    $tabMain.Controls.Add($split)

    $lv = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ListView
    $lv.View = 'Details'; $lv.CheckBoxes = $true; $lv.FullRowSelect = $true; $lv.GridLines = $true
    $lv.Dock = 'Fill'; $lv.HideSelection = $false; $lv.ShowItemToolTips = $true
    $lv.Add_DoubleClick({
        if ($script:Gui['Busy']) { Write-PatchLog 'Busy - the details window is available again when the current action finishes' 'WARN'; return }
        if ($lv.SelectedItems.Count -gt 0) { Show-ServerDetails -Name $lv.SelectedItems[0].Text }
    })
    $lv.Add_ItemChecked({ $script:Gui['CountLabel'].Text = ('{0} server row(s) shown, {1} ticked' -f $lv.Items.Count, (Get-CheckedServers).Count) })
    $split.Panel1.Controls.Add($lv)
    $script:Gui['ServerList'] = $lv

    $logBox = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.RichTextBox
    $logBox.Dock = 'Fill'; $logBox.ReadOnly = $true; $logBox.BackColor = 'White'; $logBox.WordWrap = $false
    $logBox.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Consolas', 9)
    $split.Panel2.Controls.Add($logBox)
    $script:Gui['LogBox'] = $logBox

    # ---- right panel: patches + the big buttons ----
    $right = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $right.Dock = 'Right'; $right.Width = 350; $right.Padding = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Padding(8)
    $tabMain.Controls.Add($right)

    $lblP = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $lblP.Text = 'Patches found in \patches  (tick the ones to install):'; $lblP.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(10, 8); $lblP.AutoSize = $true
    $right.Controls.Add($lblP)
    $patchList = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.CheckedListBox
    $patchList.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(10, 30); $patchList.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(325, 150); $patchList.CheckOnClick = $true
    $right.Controls.Add($patchList)
    $script:Gui['PatchList'] = $patchList
    $lblFolder = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $lblFolder.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(10, 184); $lblFolder.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(325, 32); $lblFolder.ForeColor = 'Gray'
    $right.Controls.Add($lblFolder)
    $script:Gui['PatchFolderLabel'] = $lblFolder

    $right.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Open patches' -X 10 -Y 218 -W 100 -ReadOnly -Tip 'Opens the \patches folder in Explorer' -OnClick { Invoke-Item -LiteralPath $script:Config.PatchFolder }))
    $right.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Today''s log' -X 115 -Y 218 -W 100 -ReadOnly -Tip 'Opens logs\Patcher-YYYYMMDD.log in Notepad' -OnClick {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Get-PatchLogPath))) { Write-PatchLog 'Log file created' 'INFO' }
        Start-Process notepad.exe -ArgumentList ('"{0}"' -f (Get-PatchLogPath)) }))
    $right.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Where do I get patches?' -X 220 -Y 218 -W 115 -ReadOnly -Tip 'Update history page -> KB number -> Microsoft Update Catalog -> \patches' -OnClick {
        $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'Finding and downloading patches' -Text $script:PatchHowTo }))

    $btnPatch = New-GuiButton -Text 'PATCH IT!  (ticked KBs -> ticked servers)' -X 10 -Y 268 -W 325 -H 60 -Colour 'Tomato' -Tip 'Runs the pre-flight, shows the plan, then the two safety pop-ups' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'Install' -Action {
            $servers = Get-CheckedServers; $patches = Get-CheckedPatches
            if ($servers.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Tick at least one server first.' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            if ($patches.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Tick at least one patch first.' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            # Only real result objects count (anything else in the output stream would be a leaked pop-up value).
            $results = @(Install-PatchOnServers -ComputerName $servers -Patches $patches | Where-Object { $_ -is [psobject] -and $_.PSObject.Properties['Success'] })
            if ($results.Count -gt 0) {
                $good = @($results | Where-Object { $_.Success }).Count
                $bad  = @($results | Where-Object { -not $_.Success }).Count
                $reb  = @($results | Where-Object { $_.RebootRequired }).Count
                if ($bad -eq 0) { Write-PatchLog ('   \o/  All installs succeeded. Nice one, {0}!' -f $script:Config.OperatorName) 'OK' }
                $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Title 'Install finished' -Text ("Installed OK: {0}`nFailed or unknown: {1}`nNeed a reboot: {2}`n`nDetails are in the log. Reboot with the 'Reboot ticked servers' button when you are ready." -f $good, $bad, $reb)
            }
        }
    }
    $btnPatch.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 11, [System.Drawing.FontStyle]::Bold)
    $right.Controls.Add($btnPatch)

    $right.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Reboot ticked servers' -X 10 -Y 338 -W 325 -H 34 -Colour 'Khaki' -Tip 'Fresh status first; only servers PENDING a reboot by default; refused while DISM is running.' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'Reboot' -Action {
            $servers = Get-CheckedServers
            if ($servers.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Tick at least one server first.' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            Restart-PatchedServers -ComputerName $servers
        }
    }))
    $right.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Test WinRM port (no auth) on ticked' -X 10 -Y 378 -W 325 -H 30 -ReadOnly -Tip 'Test-WSMan: is 5985 open and answering? Needs no credentials. Works during an install.' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'WinRM test' -ReadOnly -Action {
            $servers = Get-CheckedServers
            if ($servers.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Tick at least one server first.' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            foreach ($s in $servers) { Test-ServerWinRM -ComputerName $s | Out-Null }
        }
    }))

    $legend = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $legend.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(10, 420); $legend.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(325, 190); $legend.ForeColor = 'DimGray'
    $legend.Text = @"
Row colours:
  White        - not checked yet
  Grey         - WinRM failed (hover for the reason)
  Pink         - pending reboot = cannot patch
  Yellow       - at least one KB is READY to install
  Green        - every KB in \patches is installed

KB columns: Installed / Installed (history) / READY /
  Blocked: reboot / servicing / disk / signature /
  OS unknown / wrong OS  /  ? = unreachable
Build = real patch level. "PFRO only, ignored" = a weak
reboot hint, not counted (Code Tour explains).
Double-click a row for full details.
While an install runs: status checks, WinRM test, the
group box and the log still work; the rest is locked.
Console window behind me = the same log, in colour.
"@
    $right.Controls.Add($legend)

    # ---- toolbar ----
    $toolbar = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $toolbar.Dock = 'Top'; $toolbar.Height = 44
    $tabMain.Controls.Add($toolbar)
    $lblG = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label; $lblG.Text = 'Group:'; $lblG.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(8, 13); $lblG.AutoSize = $true
    $toolbar.Controls.Add($lblG)
    $combo = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ComboBox
    $combo.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(55, 9); $combo.Width = 170; $combo.DropDownStyle = 'DropDownList'
    $combo.Add_SelectedIndexChanged({ Update-ServerList })
    $toolbar.Controls.Add($combo)
    $script:Gui['GroupCombo'] = $combo

    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Reload lists + patches' -X 235 -Y 8 -W 150 -Tip 'Re-reads the *.txt group files and the patches folder' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'Reload' -Action { Initialize-PatcherData }
    }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Check status (ticked)' -X 390 -Y 8 -W 150 -Colour 'LightSkyBlue' -ReadOnly -Tip 'WinRM status check of the ticked servers. Works during an install.' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'Status check' -ReadOnly -Action {
            $servers = Get-CheckedServers
            if ($servers.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'Tick at least one server first (or use "Check ALL shown").' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $servers | Out-Null
        }
    }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Check ALL shown' -X 545 -Y 8 -W 120 -Colour 'LightSkyBlue' -ReadOnly -Tip 'Works during an install.' -OnClick {
        Invoke-GuiAction -Name 'Status check' -ReadOnly -Action {
            $all = @(Get-UniqueNames ($script:Gui['ServerList'].Items | ForEach-Object { $_.Text }))
            if ($all.Count -eq 0) { $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text 'No servers in the list. Add names to a PatchGroup-*.txt file and reload.' -Icon 'Warning'; return }
            Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName $all | Out-Null
        }
    }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Tick all shown' -X 680 -Y 8 -W 100 -ReadOnly -OnClick { foreach ($i in $script:Gui['ServerList'].Items) { $i.Checked = $true } }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Untick all' -X 785 -Y 8 -W 90 -ReadOnly -OnClick { foreach ($i in $script:Gui['ServerList'].Items) { $i.Checked = $false } }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Set credentials' -X 890 -Y 8 -W 110 -Tip 'Foreground Get-Credential prompt. Only needed if your login is refused.' -OnClick { Get-PatcherCredential -Reason 'alternate account for WinRM' | Out-Null }))
    $toolbar.Controls.Add((New-GuiButton -Text 'Clear creds' -X 1005 -Y 8 -W 85 -OnClick { Clear-PatcherCredential }))
    $countLabel = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $countLabel.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(1100, 13); $countLabel.AutoSize = $true; $countLabel.ForeColor = 'DimGray'
    $toolbar.Controls.Add($countLabel)
    $script:Gui['CountLabel'] = $countLabel

    # ---- banner ----
    $banner = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $banner.Dock = 'Top'; $banner.Height = 64; $banner.BackColor = 'MidnightBlue'
    $tabMain.Controls.Add($banner)
    $title = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $title.Text = "$($script:Config.OperatorName.ToUpper())'S PATCH PALACE"; $title.ForeColor = 'Gold'; $title.AutoSize = $true
    $title.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 20, [System.Drawing.FontStyle]::Bold)
    $title.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(12, 6)
    $title.Add_Click({ $script:Gui['QuipLabel'].Text = Get-RandomQuip })
    $banner.Controls.Add($title)
    $quip = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $quip.Text = Get-RandomQuip; $quip.ForeColor = 'White'; $quip.AutoSize = $true
    $quip.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 10, [System.Drawing.FontStyle]::Italic)
    $quip.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(400, 24)
    $banner.Controls.Add($quip)
    $script:Gui['QuipLabel'] = $quip
    $split.BringToFront()

    # ================= CODE TOUR TAB =================
    $tourSplit = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.SplitContainer
    $tourSplit.Dock = 'Fill'; $tourSplit.Orientation = 'Vertical'
    $tabTour.Controls.Add($tourSplit)
    $tourList = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.ListBox
    $tourList.Dock = 'Fill'; $tourList.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Segoe UI', 10)
    foreach ($entry in $script:CodeTour) { [void]$tourList.Items.Add($entry.Title) }
    $tourSplit.Panel1.Controls.Add($tourList)
    $tourText = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.RichTextBox
    $tourText.Dock = 'Fill'; $tourText.ReadOnly = $true; $tourText.BackColor = 'White'; $tourText.WordWrap = $false
    $tourText.Font = New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Consolas', 10)

    # Picture entries: a panel above the text that holds the PNG (hidden for text-only entries).
    $picHost = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $picHost.Dock = 'Top'; $picHost.Height = 420; $picHost.Visible = $false; $picHost.BackColor = 'White'
    $picBar = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $picBar.Dock = 'Top'; $picBar.Height = 30
    $picActual = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.CheckBox
    $picActual.Text = 'Actual size (scroll)'; $picActual.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(8, 6); $picActual.AutoSize = $true
    $picActual.Add_CheckedChanged({ Set-CodeTourPictureMode })
    $picOpen = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Button
    $picOpen.Text = 'Open picture'; $picOpen.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(160, 3); $picOpen.Size = New-Object System.Drawing.Size(100, 24)
    $picOpen.Add_Click({ if ($script:Gui['TourPicPath']) { Start-Process $script:Gui['TourPicPath'] } })
    $picLabel = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Label
    $picLabel.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(275, 8); $picLabel.AutoSize = $true; $picLabel.ForeColor = 'DimGray'
    $picBar.Controls.AddRange(@($picActual, $picOpen, $picLabel))
    $picScroll = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel
    $picScroll.Dock = 'Fill'; $picScroll.AutoScroll = $true
    $pic = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.PictureBox
    $pic.Dock = 'Fill'; $pic.SizeMode = 'Zoom'
    $pic.Add_DoubleClick({ if ($script:Gui['TourPicPath']) { Start-Process $script:Gui['TourPicPath'] } })
    $picScroll.Controls.Add($pic)
    $picHost.Controls.Add($picScroll); $picHost.Controls.Add($picBar)
    $picScroll.BringToFront()

    $tourSplit.Panel2.Controls.Add($tourText)
    $tourSplit.Panel2.Controls.Add($picHost)
    $tourText.BringToFront()
    $tourSplit.Panel2.Add_Resize({ Set-CodeTourPictureSize })
    $tourList.Add_SelectedIndexChanged({
        $entry = $script:CodeTour[$tourList.SelectedIndex]
        if ($entry) { Show-CodeTourEntry -Entry $entry }
    })
    $script:Gui['TourList'] = $tourList; $script:Gui['TourText'] = $tourText; $script:Gui['TourPanel2'] = $tourSplit.Panel2
    $script:Gui['TourPicHost'] = $picHost; $script:Gui['TourPic'] = $pic; $script:Gui['TourPicLabel'] = $picLabel
    $script:Gui['TourPicScroll'] = $picScroll; $script:Gui['TourPicActual'] = $picActual

    $form.Controls.Add($tabs)
    $form.Controls.Add($strip)
    $tabs.BringToFront()
    $form.Add_Shown({
        try { $split.SplitterDistance = [int]($split.Height * 0.6); $tourSplit.SplitterDistance = 300 } catch { }
        $tourList.SelectedIndex = 0
    })
    # Closing the window while a copy or install is running would leave sessions and DISM to their fate.
    $form.Add_FormClosing({
        if ($script:Gui['Busy']) {
            $_.Cancel = $true
            Write-PatchLog "Close refused - still busy with '$($script:Gui['BusyName'])'. Wait for it to finish, then close." 'WARN'
            $null = Show-PatcherMessage -Text "Still busy with '$($script:Gui['BusyName'])'. Wait for it to finish before closing." -Title 'Busy' -Icon 'Warning'
        }
    })

    # ---- load the data and go ----
    Write-PatchLog ("Welcome, {0}! Root folder = {1}   (running as {2})" -f $script:Config.OperatorName, $script:RootFolder, (Get-OperatorIdentity)) 'INFO'
    Initialize-PatcherData
    if ($NoShow) { return $form }
    Write-PatchLog 'GUI is open. This console window keeps a colour copy of everything.' 'INFO'
    try {
        [void]$form.ShowDialog()
    } finally {
        $form.Dispose()
        # In paste / Invoke-Expression mode $script: is the console's global scope - do not leave a password behind.
        if ($script:Credential) { Clear-PatcherCredential }
        Write-PatchLog 'GUI closed. Bye!' 'INFO'
    }
}

function Show-CodeTourEntry {
    # Fills the Code Tour right-hand side: the explanation (+ live source) and, for picture entries, the PNG.
    param($Entry)
    $text = $script:Gui['TourText']; $picHost = $script:Gui['TourPicHost']; $pic = $script:Gui['TourPic']
    $text.Text = Get-CodeTourText -Entry $Entry
    if ($pic.Image) { $old = $pic.Image; $pic.Image = $null; $old.Dispose() }
    if ($script:Gui['TourPicStream']) { $script:Gui['TourPicStream'].Dispose(); $script:Gui['TourPicStream'] = $null }
    $script:Gui['TourPicPath'] = $null
    if (-not $Entry.Image) { $picHost.Visible = $false; return }

    $path = Join-Path $script:RootFolder $Entry.Image
    if (-not (Test-Path -Path $path)) {
        $text.Text = "PICTURE NOT FOUND: $path`r`nRun Build-Diagrams.ps1 in the root folder to draw it, then come back.`r`n`r`n" + $text.Text
        $picHost.Visible = $false
        return
    }
    # Load through a MemoryStream so the PNG file is not locked while the GUI is open.
    $stream = New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream -ArgumentList (, [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path))
    $pic.Image = [System.Drawing.Image]::FromStream($stream)
    $script:Gui['TourPicStream'] = $stream
    $script:Gui['TourPicPath'] = $path
    $script:Gui['TourPicLabel'].Text = ('{0}   {1}x{2} px   (double-click the picture to open it full size)' -f $Entry.Image, $pic.Image.Width, $pic.Image.Height)
    $picHost.Visible = $true
    Set-CodeTourPictureMode
    Set-CodeTourPictureSize
}

function Set-CodeTourPictureSize {
    # The picture takes the top of the panel, the caption keeps about 190 px underneath.
    $picHost = $script:Gui['TourPicHost']; $panel = $script:Gui['TourPanel2']
    if (-not $picHost -or -not $picHost.Visible) { return }
    $picHost.Height = [math]::Max(200, $panel.ClientSize.Height - 190)
}

function Set-CodeTourPictureMode {
    # Zoom-to-fit (default) or actual size with scroll bars.
    $pic = $script:Gui['TourPic']; $scroll = $script:Gui['TourPicScroll']; $actual = $script:Gui['TourPicActual']
    if (-not $pic) { return }
    if ($actual.Checked) {
        $pic.Dock = 'None'; $pic.SizeMode = 'AutoSize'; $pic.Location = New-Object System.Drawing.Point(0, 0)
        $scroll.AutoScroll = $true
    } else {
        $pic.Dock = 'Fill'; $pic.SizeMode = 'Zoom'
        $scroll.AutoScroll = $false
    }
}

function Initialize-PatcherData {
    # Reads the group files and the patch folder, then refreshes both lists.
    Get-PatchGroups | Out-Null
    Get-PatchFiles  | Out-Null
    $combo = $script:Gui['GroupCombo']
    $keep = [string]$combo.SelectedItem
    $combo.Items.Clear()
    [void]$combo.Items.Add('(all groups)')
    foreach ($g in $script:Groups) { [void]$combo.Items.Add($g.Name) }
    if ($keep -and $combo.Items.Contains($keep)) { $combo.SelectedItem = $keep } else { $combo.SelectedIndex = 0 }
    Update-PatchList
    Update-ServerList
}
# ===================== END 07-Gui.ps1 =======================

# ===================== BEGIN 08-CodeTour.ps1 =====================
# =====================================================================
#  08-CodeTour.ps1  -  THE TRAINING CONTENT SHOWN IN THE "CODE TOUR" TAB
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Each entry = a Title, an Explain text, the name of the function (or
#  script block variable) whose LIVE source is printed underneath, and
#  optionally an Image (a PNG in images\, drawn by Build-Diagrams.ps1).
#  "Live" means it is read from memory with Get-Command, so what you see
#  is exactly what is running - even if somebody edited a file.
# =====================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REVIEW RECORD  -  08-CodeTour.ps1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Independent review 2026-10-14 (see CODE-REVIEW.md).  Changed here:
#  R-31 text that disagreed with the code (slice size 224 KB not 240,
#  plan rule order, "press Reload" for config edits, "failed at" in
#  all-in-one mode, Kerberos/FQDN/TrustedHosts wording) and new topics
#  for the guards added by the review.  Text only - nothing here runs
#  on a server.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HUMAN REVIEW  (fill in by hand and keep it in the file)
#  Reviewer   : ______________________________   Date : ______________
#  Verdict    : [ ] Approved   [ ] Approved with comments   [ ] Changes required
#  Checked    : [ ] every topic read against the live source it shows
#  Comments   :
#    -
# =====================================================================

$script:CodeTour = @(
    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '0. Start here - the big picture'; Source = ''; Explain = @'
WHAT THIS TOOL DOES
  1. Reads server lists  : every *.txt file in the root folder (PatchGroup-A.txt ...)
  2. Reads patch files   : every .msu / .cab in \patches - KB from the name, target build,
     Microsoft signature and SHA256 from inside the file (cached in patches\_info)
  3. Asks each server over WinRM (TCP 5985): build, free disk, installed hotfixes,
     Windows Update history, pending reboot, servicing in progress.
     Shows per KB: Installed / READY / Blocked: <why>.
  4. Installs a KB on ticked servers after THREE confirmations:
     the plan, "VMware snapshot taken?", "Trellix in maintenance mode?".
     Answer No to either safety question and nothing happens.

THE FILES (root folder)
  Start-OfflinePatcher.ps1   the launcher - checks the folder, loads lib\*.ps1 (explicit list)
  lib\01-Config.ps1          settings + shared variables ($Config, $ServerStatus ...)
  lib\02-Logging.ps1         Write-PatchLog: file + console + GUI, colour coded; audit identity
  lib\03-Groups.ps1          Get-PatchGroups: parse the *.txt lists
  lib\04-Patches.ps1         Get-PatchFiles : scan \patches, read build/signature/hash; Get-PatchVerdict
  lib\05-WinRM.ps1           status check, credentials, Test-WSMan, the slice copy
  lib\06-Install.ps1         safety pop-ups, plan, locked staging folder, DISM install, reboot
  lib\07-Gui.ps1             the window you are looking at
  lib\08-CodeTour.ps1        this text
  Build-TextCopies.ps1       makes the .txt versions (code-as-text\ + the all-in-one)
  Build-Diagrams.ps1         draws the pictures in images\
  CODE-REVIEW.md             the independent review: every finding, what was done, sign-off
  Every .ps1 starts with a REVIEW RECORD block with space for a human reviewer.

RUNNING IT WITHOUT A GUI (handy for fault finding)
  cd to the root folder, then in PowerShell 5.1 load the building blocks only:
     $NoGui = $true
     . .\Start-OfflinePatcher.ps1
  (or, if .ps1 files are blocked:  $NoGui = $true; Invoke-Expression (Get-Content -Raw .\Offline-Patcher-AllInOne.txt))
  then call any function by hand:
     Get-PatchGroups; Get-PatchFiles
     Get-ServerStatus -ComputerName SRV01     # everything is logged to logs\
     $ServerStatus['SRV01'] | Format-List     # raw result
     & $RemoteStatusScript $false             # run the remote status block on THIS machine
     Show-PatcherGui                          # open the window when you are ready

LOG LEVELS
  CMD  = the exact command sent - copy it into a console to reproduce by hand
  WHY  = the reasoning behind the next step
  Every INSTALL / CONFIRM / RESULT / REBOOT line names the operator (audit trail).
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '0a. PICTURE: the big picture'; Source = ''; Image = 'images\1-big-picture.png'; Explain = @'
Who talks to whom.  Three machines matter: the INTERNET PC where the .msu is downloaded
(any PC, the tool is not involved), the OPERATOR PC where this tool runs, and the TARGET
SERVERS from the group files.  Only one connection is made by the tool: operator PC ->
server on TCP 5985, WinRM over HTTP, authenticated with Kerberos (use FQDNs in the group
files; an IP address forces NTLM and would need TrustedHosts - never set that to *).
The domain controller is already in the picture for DNS and Kerberos; nothing new is
opened.  The red box lists what the tool deliberately never uses, which is also the
answer to "what do I need to allow through the firewall?": 5985 and nothing else.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '0b. PICTURE: ports and protocols'; Source = ''; Image = 'images\2-ports-and-protocols.png'; Explain = @'
The table is the firewall conversation in one page.  Below it, the layers inside 5985
from the outside in - HTTP, then the WS-Management SOAP envelope (whose size limit,
MaxEnvelopeSizekb, is why files are copied in slices), then PSRP carrying our commands,
then wsmprovhost.exe on the server actually running them.  The yellow box lists the
only WinRM settings on a server that ever matter to this tool.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '1. Config - settings and shared state'; Source = 'Config'; Explain = @'
$script:Config is a plain hashtable, filled when the tool starts.  To change a value for
good, edit lib\01-Config.ps1 and start the tool again.  To try a value right now, type in
the console behind the GUI, e.g.  $Config.MinFreeGB = 8  - it takes effect at the next
status check.  "Reload lists + patches" re-reads the group files and \patches only.
  WinRMPort 5985      -> the HTTP WinRM listener (5986 would be HTTPS)
  OpenTimeoutSec      -> how long a silent server is given before we call it unreachable
  MaxParallel         -> servers checked at the same time (ThrottleLimit)
  RemoteStaging       -> folder created on the target where the .msu is copied (ACL locked down)
  MinFreeGB           -> below this the install is refused (DISM needs room)
  RequireValidSignature  -> the .msu must be Authenticode-signed by Microsoft (checked twice)
  AllowUnknownTargetBuild -> off: a file whose build cannot be read is blocked
  TreatPendingFileRenameAsReboot -> PendingFileRenameOperations is set by many
                         installers and AV products; it is NOT counted as "pending
                         reboot" unless you flip this to $true.
  ProgressEverySec / InstallTimeoutMin -> the install wait loop
Shared state: $script:Credential (memory only, cleared when the GUI closes),
$script:ServerStatus (name -> last result), $script:Groups, $script:Patches,
$script:Gui (the WinForms controls), $script:Operator (who is running the tool).
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '1a. PICTURE: the folder on the operator PC'; Source = ''; Image = 'images\3-operator-folder.png'; Explain = @'
Every file in the root folder and its one job.  lib\ is loaded in number order from an
explicit list; patches\ is yours to fill; logs\ is written by the tool; the .txt twins and
the all-in-one file exist for machines that block .ps1 scripts by ExecutionPolicy (not
AppLocker - see topic 16).  The yellow box lists the variables you can inspect from the
console while the GUI is open ($ServerStatus, $Patches, $Config ...).
TRUST BOUNDARY: everything in this folder runs as you on every server.  Keep the folder
writable only by the operators.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '2. Write-PatchLog - one log, three outputs'; Source = 'Write-PatchLog'; Explain = @'
Every message goes to logs\Patcher-YYYYMMDD.log, to the console (colour) and to the
GUI log box.  The GUI part calls Application.DoEvents() so the window repaints while
a long job runs - that is the trick that keeps a single-threaded WinForms script alive.
AUDIT: the session header and every INSTALL / CONFIRM / RESULT / REBOOT line carry the
operator identity from Get-OperatorIdentity ("DOMAIN\user", plus "(WinRM as X)" when
alternate credentials are in use).  Each install also writes Application event 900
(source OfflinePatcher) and a result-*.txt on the server itself.  Passwords are never
logged anywhere.
FAULT FINDING: the log file is plain text; search for [ERROR] or for a server name.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '3. Get-PatchGroups - reading the server lists'; Source = 'Get-PatchGroups'; Explain = @'
Any *.txt in the root folder is a candidate.  A line is a host name if it only has
letters, digits, dots and dashes.  Comments start with #.  If ANY line fails that
test the file is ignored (that is how the code-as-text copies are kept out).
The file name without .txt is the group name shown in the Group drop-down.
Names are de-duplicated case-insensitively (Get-UniqueNames), an IP address gets a
warning (no Kerberos), and the same first label written two ways (SRV01 and
srv01.corp.local) is flagged - the install de-duplicates again by the server's real
name after the status check so one box is never patched twice at once.
FAULT FINDING: a group missing from the drop-down?  Look for "Ignoring ... not a
server list" in the log - it names the offending line.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '4. Get-PatchFiles - scanning \patches'; Source = 'Get-PatchFiles'; Explain = @'
Looks for .msu and .cab files.  The KB number is pulled from the FILE NAME with the
regex (KB\d{6,7}), so keep the Microsoft Update Catalog name, e.g.
   windows10.0-kb5034770-x64_....msu   ->  KB5034770
A file without a KB in its name is skipped with a warning - just rename it.
For every file Get-PatchFileInfo reads, once, and caches in patches\_info\<file>.txt
(re-read when the size or date changes):
  TARGET BUILD   The name alone cannot say: Server 2016, 2019 and 2022 all use
                 "windows10.0-kb..." names.  expand.exe pulls the small .xml out of the
                 MSU (package versions like 20348.5614.1.3), or pkgProperties.txt
                 (Installer Version="10.0.20348.x"), or the SSU cab name.  14393 = 2016,
                 17763 = 2019, 20348 = 2022, 26100 = 2025.  Unknown = blocked, because
                 the file-name fallback cannot tell 2019 from 2022.
  SIGNATURE      Get-AuthenticodeSignature must say Valid AND the signer must be
                 Microsoft, otherwise "Blocked: signature".  Works offline.
  SHA256         used to verify the copy on the server and again right before DISM.
Mixed groups are fine: put the 2019 and the 2022 cumulative updates in \patches
together and each server gets a READY only in its own column.  DISM is the last line
of defence anyway - it refuses a wrong package with 0x800F081E.
This tool is OFFLINE: nothing is ever downloaded; you put the files there.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '4b. Finding this month''s patch (catalog how-to)'; Source = ''; Explain = $script:PatchHowTo }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '5. RemoteStatusScript - what runs ON the server'; Source = 'RemoteStatusScript'; Explain = @'
This script block is shipped to each server by Invoke-Command and executed there.
It must be self contained: it cannot see our functions or variables, only the
parameter passed with -ArgumentList.  It is READ-ONLY.
  Win32_OperatingSystem       -> caption, last boot time
  HKLM\...\CurrentVersion     -> CurrentBuildNumber + UBR  = e.g. 20348.2322
  Win32_LogicalDisk C:        -> free space
  Get-HotFix                  -> installed KB list (primary "is it installed?" source).  Only CBS
                                 packages still on disk: superseded cumulative updates drop off,
                                 so expect a SHORT list (current LCU, SSU, .NET, a few more).
  Microsoft.Update.Session    -> Windows Update Agent history = Settings > Update history.
     QueryHistory               Every install attempt ever, newest first (80 shown).  Read from
                                 the local database over COM, nothing goes online.  A KB whose
                                 newest entry is a successful Install counts as installed too.
  Registry keys               -> pending reboot.  HARD signs, always counted:
                                 CBS\RebootPending, CBS\PackagesPending, CBS\RebootInProgress,
                                 WU\RebootRequired, WU\PostRebootReporting, UpdateExeVolatile,
                                 a pending computer rename.
                                 WEAK sign, shown but not counted: PendingFileRenameOperations
                                 (PFRO) = files to rename/delete at next boot because they were
                                 locked.  AV products and installers add to it constantly and it
                                 is often left behind, hence "no (PFRO only, ignored)" in the grid.
  ServicingActive             -> somebody is servicing the box right now (another admin, Windows
                                 Update, a previous run).  Blocks installs and reboots.  Counted:
                                 dism.exe or wusa.exe running; TiWorker.exe ONLY while it is burning
                                 CPU (sampled over 2 s - it idles for minutes after routine
                                 maintenance, which is not servicing); the Windows Update agent's
                                 own "installing" flag (IUpdateInstaller.IsBusy).  A "Blocked:
                                 servicing" normally clears within a few minutes - re-check.
  Both update lists are sent as pre-formatted text lines because PowerShell remoting
  flattens nested objects to strings (serialization depth 1).
  WHICH KB IS "THE" PATCH LEVEL?  None - the BUILD is.  The UBR (number after the dot in
  20348.5622) changes with every cumulative update and only moves after the reboot.  The
  "Newest hotfixes" column lists all Get-HotFix entries from the latest install date because
  the cumulative update and the .NET cumulative update land on the same day with different KBs.
Run it on THIS machine from the console to see the raw output:   & $RemoteStatusScript $false
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '6. Get-ServerStatus - fan-out over WinRM'; Source = 'Get-ServerStatus'; Explain = @'
One Invoke-Command with -ComputerName <many> -AsJob gives a parent job with one child
job per server, all running at the same time (up to MaxParallel).  We wait with
Wait-PatcherJob (which keeps the GUI alive and treats only Completed / Failed /
Stopped / Disconnected as finished), then harvest each child:
  * output received  -> reachable, store the object + Reachable/Error/Checked
  * no output        -> unreachable, store the full error text (one line)
If a server answered "Access is denied" and no credential is stored yet, the tool
asks ONCE with Get-Credential (foreground) and retries just those servers.
FAULT FINDING: the CMD line in the log shows exactly what was sent.  Typical errors:
  "WinRM cannot complete the operation"  -> port 5985 blocked or service stopped
  "Access is denied"                     -> account is not an admin on that server
  "Kerberos ... "                        -> use the FQDN in the group file.  Do NOT "fix"
                                            it with TrustedHosts=*; that turns off the
                                            check that you are talking to the right server.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '6a. PICTURE: a status check, step by step'; Source = ''; Image = 'images\4-status-check.png'; Explain = @'
Three lanes: operator PC, the wire, target server.  One Invoke-Command fans out to every
server at once; on each server RemoteStatusScript reads the OS, build, disk, both update
lists, the reboot flags and the servicing processes - read-only, 2-5 seconds - and one
result object comes back per server.  The two branches at the bottom are the only things
that ever go wrong at this stage: "Access is denied" (credential prompt, foreground) and
"no answer" (grey row, Test-WSMan button).
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '7. Credentials - foreground only'; Source = 'Get-PatcherCredential'; Explain = @'
The tool never stores passwords on disk.  Get-Credential shows the standard Windows
dialog in the foreground, in the logged-on user's context.  The dialog belongs to the
console window, so it can appear BEHIND the GUI - the status bar says so, and the GUI is
brought back to the front afterwards.  If you cancel, the tool keeps using your current
Windows login (Kerberos single sign-on).  The credential is cleared from memory when the
GUI closes, so nothing is left behind in a pasted / Invoke-Expression console.
Get-ConnectionArgs builds the same -Port / -SessionOption / -Credential set for every
call so all WinRM traffic is uniform.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '8. Test-ServerWinRM - the no-auth check'; Source = 'Test-ServerWinRM'; Explain = @'
Test-WSMan sends a WS-Management "Identify" request.  WinRM answers it anonymously,
which is why "winrm get/enumerate" style calls worked without credentials in testing.
It proves: DNS resolves, TCP 5985 is open, the WinRM service is running.
It does NOT prove you are allowed in - that needs Invoke-Command.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '9. Confirm-SafetyChecks - the two pop-ups'; Source = 'Confirm-SafetyChecks'; Explain = @'
Pop-up 1: "Has a VMware snapshot been taken?"      Yes / No
Pop-up 2: "Is Trellix in maintenance mode?"        Yes / No
The default button is No, so pressing Enter by accident can never approve.
Either No -> the function returns $false, Install-PatchOnServers returns without
opening a single session, and an [ERROR] ABORTED line with the operator's name goes in
the log.  With many servers the pop-up becomes a scrollable window with the same buttons.
A LESSON FROM THE REVIEW: a MessageBox RETURNS the button pressed.  The first version
showed an extra "Patching aborted" box without capturing its result, so the function
returned @('OK', $false) - which PowerShell treats as TRUE - and the install went ahead
after a No.  Every pop-up whose answer is not needed is now written  $null = Show-...
and the caller checks for a real [bool] $true.  Watch for this pattern in any script.
'@ }

    [pscustomobject]@{ Title = '10. Get-PatchVerdict - can it be installed?'; Source = 'Get-PatchVerdict'; Explain = @'
ONE function decides, and both the grid cell and the install plan call it, so they can
